subproblems.title: Mass of an integer multiplicity current equals its representing measure, and its support is the support of that measure
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P (= Euclid P) be open, let T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n) and let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an integer multiplicity representation of T in U (an IMRep U n with R.Represents T, i.e. T(ω) = ∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(x)) dH^n(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U), where H^n = μHE[n]). Write μ_R := R.measure = θ·H^n⌞M. Then: (a) M_W(T) = μ_R(W) for every open W ⊆ U, where M_W(T) = T.massOn W is the supremum (in [0, ∞]) of ofReal T(ω) over ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W and Euclidean coefficient norm |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x; (b) for every x ∈ U: x ∈ spt T if and only if μ_R(B_ε(x)) ≠ 0 for every ε > 0; (c) every other representation R' of T has the same measure: R'.measure = R.measure.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : IMRep U n), IsOpen U → R.Represents T → (∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → W ⊆ U → T.massOn W = R.measure W) ∧ (∀ x ∈ U, (x ∈ T.support ↔ ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → R.measure (ball x ε) ≠ 0)) ∧ ∀ R' : IMRep U n, R'.Represents T → R'.measure = R.measure
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, 2.4–2.8 and Remark 3.2(3) (chapter-06.txt lines 224–300 and 733–775), which state these facts as evident; this is the identity "μ_S = R.measure for every representation R, M_W(S) = μ_S(W), spt S = spt μ_S" used throughout the parent proof (its Notation paragraph). Notation: H^n := μHE[n]; for an n-covector α on ℝ^P, |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_I α(e_{i_1}, …, e_{i_n})²)^{1/2}, the sum over strictly increasing multi-indices I = (i_1 < ⋯ < i_n) (for n = 0, |α| = |α()|); dx^I is the dual basis covector.
1. (Pointwise duality.) Let τ_1, …, τ_n ∈ ℝ^P be orthonormal and let α be an n-covector. By multilinearity and alternation, α(τ_1, …, τ_n) = Σ_I α(e_I)·det(τ^I), where τ^I is the n × n matrix (⟨e_{i_a}, τ_b⟩)_{a,b}. By the Cauchy–Binet formula, Σ_I det(τ^I)² = det(τᵀτ) = det(I_n) = 1. Hence |α(τ_1, …, τ_n)| ≤ |α| by the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality, with equality for α_τ := Σ_I det(τ^I) dx^I, which satisfies |α_τ| = 1 and α_τ(τ_1, …, τ_n) = 1. (For n = 0 both sides equal |α()| and α_τ := 1.)
2. (Consequences for R.) By the field `orients` of IMRep, for H^n-a.e. x ∈ M there are an orthonormal family τ(x) and a sign σ(x) ∈ {±1} with ξ(x)(α) = σ(x)·α(τ(x)) for every n-covector α (IsUnitOrientationOf). Hence, for H^n-a.e. x ∈ M, |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for all α. Moreover β(x) := Σ_I ξ(x)(dx^I)·dx^I equals σ(x)·α_{τ(x)} for H^n-a.e. x ∈ M, so |β(x)| = 1 and ξ(x)(β(x)) = 1 there. The coefficients ξ(·)(dx^I) of β are H^n⌞M-measurable because ξ is AEStronglyMeasurable for H^n⌞M (field aestronglyMeasurable_orient); as μ_R ≪ H^n⌞M, β is μ_R-measurable.
3. (Radon property.) μ_R is a Borel measure on ℝ^P with μ_R(ℝ^P ∖ U) = 0 (M ⊆ U) and μ_R(K) = ∫_{M∩K} θ dH^n < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U (field locallyIntegrable_mult). Since U is an open subset of ℝ^P, hence σ-compact, locally compact and second countable, the restriction of μ_R to U is a locally finite Borel measure on U and therefore outer regular by open sets and inner regular by compact sets on Borel subsets of U.
4. (Upper bound in (a).) Let W ⊆ U be open and let ω be admissible for M_W(T) (ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U), tsupport ω ⊆ W, |ω| ≤ 1 everywhere). By R.Represents T and step 2, T(ω) = ∫_M θ·ξ(ω) dH^n ≤ ∫_M θ·|ω| dH^n ≤ ∫_{M∩W} θ dH^n = μ_R(W), because ω vanishes off W. Taking ofReal and the supremum, M_W(T) ≤ μ_R(W).
5. (Lower bound in (a).) Let W ⊆ U be open, K ⊆ W compact and ε > 0. By step 3 choose an open V with K ⊆ V, closure V compact and contained in W, and μ_R(V ∖ K) < ε. By Lusin's theorem (for the finite Radon measure μ_R⌞V and the μ_R-measurable map β of step 2, with values in the finite-dimensional space Λ^n of n-covectors) choose a compact K' ⊆ K with μ_R(K ∖ K') < ε and β|_{K'} continuous. Extend β|_{K'} to a continuous map ℝ^P → Λ^n (Tietze, coordinatewise) and compose with the retraction r(α) := α / max(1, |α|) (continuous, |r(α)| ≤ 1, r = id on the closed unit ball) to obtain a continuous β̃ with |β̃| ≤ 1 and β̃ = β on K'. Take χ ∈ C_c(V; [0, 1]) with χ = 1 on K, and put γ := χ·β̃ (continuous, |γ| ≤ 1, compact support in V). Let γ_j := γ * ϱ_{1/j} be the coordinatewise convolution with a standard mollifier. For all large j, γ_j is C^∞, tsupport γ_j is a compact subset of V ⊆ W ⊆ U, |γ_j| ≤ 1 everywhere (Jensen's inequality for the convex function |·|), and γ_j → γ uniformly. So γ_j is admissible for M_W(T) and M_W(T) ≥ ofReal T(γ_j). By dominated convergence (dominating function θ·1_{closure V}, integrable by step 3), T(γ_j) = ∫_M θ·ξ(γ_j) dH^n → ∫_M θ·ξ(γ) dH^n. On K', ξ(γ) = ξ(β) = 1 μ_R-a.e.; on V ∖ K', |ξ(γ)| ≤ 1; off V, γ = 0. Hence ∫_M θ·ξ(γ) dH^n ≥ μ_R(K') − μ_R(V ∖ K') ≥ (μ_R(K) − ε) − 2ε, since μ_R(V ∖ K') ≤ μ_R(V ∖ K) + μ_R(K ∖ K') < 2ε. Therefore M_W(T) ≥ μ_R(K) − 3ε for every compact K ⊆ W and every ε > 0, and inner regularity of μ_R on the open set W (step 3) gives M_W(T) ≥ μ_R(W) (also when μ_R(W) = ∞). Together with step 4, M_W(T) = μ_R(W).
6. ((b), "if".) Let x ∈ U with μ_R(B_ε(x)) ≠ 0 for every ε > 0, and suppose x ∉ spt T = U ∖ zeroRegion(T). Then x ∈ W for some open W with closure W compact and contained in U on which T vanishes, i.e. T(ω) = 0 whenever tsupport ω ⊆ W. Every admissible value in the definition of M_W(T) is ofReal 0 = 0 (and the zero form is admissible), so M_W(T) = 0, and by (a) μ_R(W) = 0. For ε > 0 so small that B_ε(x) ⊆ W we get μ_R(B_ε(x)) = 0, a contradiction. Hence x ∈ spt T.
7. ((b), "only if".) Let x ∈ spt T and suppose μ_R(B_ε(x)) = 0 for some ε > 0. Choose ε' ∈ (0, ε) with closedBall x ε' ⊆ U (U is open). W := B_{ε'}(x) is open, its closure closedBall x ε' is compact and contained in U, and for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W, step 2 gives |T(ω)| ≤ ∫_{M∩W} θ·|ω| dH^n ≤ (sup_x |ω(x)|)·μ_R(W) = 0. So T vanishes on W, W belongs to the family defining zeroRegion(T), x ∈ zeroRegion(T), i.e. x ∉ spt T: a contradiction. Hence μ_R(B_ε(x)) ≠ 0 for every ε > 0.
8. ((c).) Let R' be another representation of T. By (a) applied to R and to R', R'.measure(W) = M_W(T) = R.measure(W) for every open W ⊆ U. Both measures vanish on ℝ^P ∖ U (both carriers lie in U) and are finite on every open W whose closure is a compact subset of U (step 3). The open subsets of U with compact closure in U form a π-system (closed under finite intersections) generating the Borel σ-algebra of U (every open subset of U is a countable union of them), and U is the union of an increasing sequence of them on which both measures are finite. By the uniqueness theorem for measures agreeing on such a generating π-system, R'.measure(A ∩ U) = R.measure(A ∩ U) for every Borel A, hence R'.measure = R.measure.
proof_key_steps: Cauchy–Binet duality: |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for the unit simple orientation ξ(x), with equality for the dual covector β(x).
Upper bound M_W(T) ≤ μ_R(W) directly from the representation.
Lower bound by Lusin, Tietze extension, retraction to the unit ball, mollification and inner regularity of the Radon measure μ_R.
Support: T vanishes on W ⇔ M_W(T) = 0 ⇔ μ_R(W) = 0, giving spt T = spt μ_R inside U.
Representation independence: two representations agree on open subsets of U, hence (π-system uniqueness, σ-finiteness on U) everywhere.

subproblems.title: Minimizing 0-currents supported in the constraint set vanish
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, let A ⊆ ℝ^P be an arbitrary set and let T ∈ 𝒟_0(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U 0). If T is minimizing in A (IsMinimizingIn T A, Simon 7.1.1; in degree 0 the condition ∂S = ∂T is vacuous, SameBoundary = True) and spt T ⊆ A, then T = 0.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (U A : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U 0), IsOpen U → IsMinimizingIn T A → T.support ⊆ A → T = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 0 of the parent proof (Simon 7.1.1 with Ch. 6, 3.1); the details are supplied. H^0 := μHE[0].
1. By the first conjunct of IsMinimizingIn, T is integer multiplicity; fix an IMRep R = (M, θ, ξ) in U with R.Represents T. By Mathlib, μHE[0] = μH[0] (euclideanHausdorffMeasure_zero) and μH[0]{x} = 1 (hausdorffMeasure_zero_singleton), so H^0 is the counting measure on countable sets and every point of M has H^0⌞M-measure ≥ 1. Consequently every statement that holds H^0⌞M-a.e. holds at every point of M.
2. (Local finiteness.) For every compact K ⊆ U, Σ_{x ∈ M∩K} θ(x) = ∫_{M∩K} θ dH^0 < ∞ (field locallyIntegrable_mult) and θ ≥ 1 on M (field mult_pos), so M ∩ K is finite.
3. Suppose, for a contradiction, that M ≠ ∅, and fix x₀ ∈ M. By step 1 and the field `orients`, ξ(x₀) satisfies IsUnitOrientationOf for a 0-dimensional subspace: the orthonormal family τ is empty and there is σ₀ ∈ {1, −1} with ξ(x₀)(α) = σ₀·α() for every 0-covector α.
4. Choose ε₀ > 0 with closedBall x₀ ε₀ ⊆ U. By step 2, M ∩ closedBall x₀ ε₀ is finite, so there is ε ∈ (0, ε₀) with M ∩ closedBall x₀ ε = {x₀}. Put W := B_ε(x₀). Then W is open and closure W ⊆ closedBall x₀ ε is compact and contained in U, i.e. CompactlyContained W U.
5. For every s > 0, μ_R(B_s(x₀)) ≥ θ(x₀) ≥ 1 > 0, where μ_R = R.measure. By the sibling child im_mass_measure (b), x₀ ∈ spt T, hence x₀ ∈ A.
6. (The competitor.) Define S(ω) := T(ω) − θ(x₀)·σ₀·ω(x₀)() for ω ∈ 𝒟^0(U). S is linear, and it is a GeometricCurrentOn U 0: if ω_j → 0 in the test-form topology, the ω_j converge to 0 uniformly on a compact set containing all their supports, so ω_j(x₀)() → 0 and S(ω_j) → 0. S is integer multiplicity: R' := (M ∖ {x₀}, θ, ξ) is an IMRep in U (M ∖ {x₀} is Borel and is a subset of the countably 0-rectifiable set M, hence countably 0-rectifiable; θ is measurable and positive on it; local integrability, measurability of ξ and the a.e. orientation condition are inherited from R), and R'.action(ω) = Σ_{x ∈ M ∖ {x₀}} θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(x)) = R.action(ω) − θ(x₀)σ₀ω(x₀)() = S(ω).
7. (Support of S − T.) S − T is the current ω ↦ −θ(x₀)σ₀·ω(x₀)(). It vanishes on every open set with compact closure in U not containing x₀, so every point of U ∖ {x₀} lies in zeroRegion(S − T). Every open neighbourhood W' of x₀ with compact closure in U carries a smooth compactly supported 0-form ω with tsupport ω ⊆ W' and ω(x₀)() = 1, on which (S − T)(ω) = −θ(x₀)σ₀ ≠ 0; so x₀ ∉ zeroRegion(S − T). Hence (S − T).support = {x₀}, which is compact and contained in A ∩ W (steps 4 and 5).
8. SameBoundary S T holds because the degree is 0. Applying the second conjunct of IsMinimizingIn T A to W (open, CompactlyContained W U) and the integer multiplicity S, we get M_W(T) ≤ M_W(S).
9. By im_mass_measure (a) (W is open and W ⊆ U): M_W(T) = μ_R(W) = θ(x₀) ≥ 1, since M ∩ W = {x₀}; and M_W(S) = μ_{R'}(W) = 0, since (M ∖ {x₀}) ∩ W = ∅. This contradicts step 8. Hence M = ∅, so T(ω) = R.action(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟^0(U), i.e. T = 0 (GeometricCurrentOn.ext).
proof_key_steps: A representation of a 0-current is a locally finite set with positive integer weights (H^0 is counting measure); every point carries a ± orientation.
A point x₀ of the carrier lies in spt T ⊆ A, and a small ball W isolates it.
Deleting x₀ gives an integer multiplicity competitor whose difference with T is supported in {x₀} ⊆ A ∩ W.
Mass comparison via im_mass_measure: M_W(T) = θ(x₀) ≥ 1 > 0 = M_W(S), contradicting minimality; so the carrier is empty and T = 0.

subproblems.title: Monotonicity, existence of densities and the density lower bound for minimizing cycles in a submanifold
subproblems.statement: Let P, n, d ∈ ℕ with 1 ≤ n ≤ d ≤ P, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, let N ⊆ ℝ^P be an embedded C² d-dimensional submanifold (IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 2 d N) with (closure N ∖ N) ∩ U = ∅, and let T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) be minimizing in U ∩ N (IsMinimizingIn T (U ∩ N)) with spt T ⊆ U ∩ N and ∂T = 0 in U (BoundaryVanishes T). Then: (i) for every compact K ⊆ U there is Λ ≥ 0 such that for every y ∈ ℝ^P and R > 0 with closedBall y R ⊆ K the function ρ ↦ e^{Λρ}ρ^{−n}·M_{B_ρ(y)}(T) (in [0, ∞], written ofReal(e^{Λρ}/ρ^n)·T.massOn (ball y ρ)) is nondecreasing on (0, R); (ii) if N = ℝ^P, then for every y and R with B_R(y) ⊆ U the function ρ ↦ ρ^{−n}·M_{B_ρ(y)}(T) is nondecreasing on (0, R); (iii) there is Θ : ℝ^P → ℝ with HasMassDensity T y (Θ(y)) (Θ^n(μ_T, y) = Θ(y)) for every y ∈ U and Θ upper semicontinuous on U; (iv) if y ∈ spt T and HasMassDensity T y θ, then θ ≥ 1.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent step T1, i.e. Simon Ch. 4, 3.1–3.17 and 3.11 (chapter-04.txt lines 215–430) applied to the varifold of T through the sibling minimizing_implies_stationary; the computations are written out. Write ω_n := unitBallVolume n ∈ (0, ∞).
0. (Setting.) Put k := P − n and ℓ := d − n; then P = n + k, d = n + ℓ and ℓ ≤ k. Transporting along the equality Euclid P = Euclid (n + k) (nothing else changes), the hypotheses are exactly those of the sibling minimizing_implies_stationary (DAG node root.minimizing_implies_stationary-a1, frozen type MinimizingImpliesStationary). T is integer multiplicity (first conjunct of IsMinimizingIn); fix a representation R = (M, θ, ξ) and put μ := R.measure = θ·H^n⌞M and V := v(M, θ). By the sibling, R.HasLocallyBoundedMeanCurvature: there is a μ-measurable H : ℝ^P → ℝ^P such that δV(X) := ∫ div_M X dμ = −∫ X·H dμ for every C¹ vector field X with compact support in U (div_M X(x) = trace(p_{T_xM} ∘ DX(x)), T_xM the approximate tangent plane, which exists μ-a.e.), and for every compact K ⊆ U there is Λ_K with |H| ≤ Λ_K μ-a.e. on K; and R.IsStationaryAlong N. By the sibling child im_mass_measure (a), M_W(T) = μ(W) for every open W ⊆ U; these values are finite when closure W is a compact subset of U.
1. (Differential identity; Simon 3.2–3.4 and 3.16.) Fix a compact K ⊆ U, Λ := max(Λ_K, 0), y ∈ ℝ^P and R > 0 with closedBall y R ⊆ K, ε ∈ (0, 1), and φ ∈ C¹(ℝ; [0, 1]) with φ' ≤ 0, φ = 1 on (−∞, 1] and φ = 0 on [1 + ε, ∞). For ρ ∈ (0, R/(1 + ε)) let X_ρ(x) := φ(|x − y|/ρ)(x − y), a C¹ vector field with support in closedBall y ((1 + ε)ρ) ⊆ K. With r := |x − y| and D^⊥r the component of (x − y)/r orthogonal to T_xM, at μ-a.e. x we have div_M X_ρ = n·φ(r/ρ) + (r/ρ)φ'(r/ρ)(1 − |D^⊥r|²) (Simon 3.2: ∇^M φ(r/ρ) = ρ^{−1}φ'(r/ρ) p_{T_xM}((x − y)/r) and div_M(x − y) = n). Put I(ρ) := ∫ φ(r/ρ) dμ and J(ρ) := ∫ φ(r/ρ)|D^⊥r|² dμ; both are differentiable in ρ with derivatives obtained by differentiating under the integral sign (φ' is bounded and all integrands vanish outside K). Since (r/ρ)φ'(r/ρ) = −ρ·∂_ρ[φ(r/ρ)], the identity δV(X_ρ) = −∫ X_ρ·H dμ reads n·I(ρ) − ρI'(ρ) = −ρJ'(ρ) − ∫ φ(r/ρ)(x − y)·H dμ, i.e. d/dρ(ρ^{−n}I(ρ)) = ρ^{−n}J'(ρ) + ρ^{−n−1}∫ φ(r/ρ)(x − y)·H dμ.
2. (Monotonicity on closed balls; Simon 3.17.) J is nondecreasing in ρ (φ(r/ρ) is nondecreasing in ρ because φ' ≤ 0), so J' ≥ 0. On the support of φ(r/ρ) we have |x − y| ≤ (1 + ε)ρ and |H| ≤ Λ μ-a.e., so the last term is ≥ −(1 + ε)Λρ^{−n}I(ρ). Hence d/dρ(e^{(1+ε)Λρ}ρ^{−n}I(ρ)) ≥ 0, and e^{(1+ε)Λρ}ρ^{−n}I(ρ) is nondecreasing on (0, R/(1 + ε)). Let ε ↓ 0 along a sequence of such φ = φ_ε decreasing pointwise to the indicator of (−∞, 1]; by dominated convergence I_ε(ρ) → μ(closedBall y ρ). Hence e^{Λσ}σ^{−n}μ(closedBall y σ) ≤ e^{Λρ}ρ^{−n}μ(closedBall y ρ) for 0 < σ < ρ < R. (This is the statement of SimonGMT HasGeneralizedMeanCurvatureIn.exp_normalizedBallMass_monotoneOn for the library's varifold structure.)
3. ((i).) Let 0 < σ < ρ < R and σ ≤ s < ρ. Then e^{Λσ}σ^{−n}μ(B_σ(y)) ≤ e^{Λσ}σ^{−n}μ(closedBall y σ) ≤ e^{Λs}s^{−n}μ(closedBall y s) ≤ e^{Λs}s^{−n}μ(B_ρ(y)), and letting s ↑ ρ gives e^{Λσ}σ^{−n}μ(B_σ(y)) ≤ e^{Λρ}ρ^{−n}μ(B_ρ(y)). As B_ρ(y) ⊆ K ⊆ U is open, μ(B_ρ(y)) = M_{B_ρ(y)}(T) (step 0), so ρ ↦ ofReal(e^{Λρ}/ρ^n)·M_{B_ρ(y)}(T) is nondecreasing on (0, R). Λ depends only on K, as required.
4. ((ii).) If N = ℝ^P, every vector v is tangent to N at every point (take γ(t) := x + tv in the definition of tangentSpace), so R.IsStationaryAlong N says δV(X) = 0 for every C¹ field X with compact support in U. Then steps 1–3 hold with the H-term replaced by 0, i.e. with Λ = 0, on every closed ball closedBall y R' ⊆ U. If B_R(y) ⊆ U and 0 < σ < ρ < R, choose R' ∈ (ρ, R); closedBall y R' ⊆ B_R(y) ⊆ U, and the Λ = 0 version of step 3 on (0, R') compares σ and ρ.
5. ((iii).) Let y ∈ U; choose R > 0 with K := closedBall y R ⊆ U and Λ as in (i). g(ρ) := e^{Λρ}ρ^{−n}μ(B_ρ(y)) is nondecreasing, nonnegative and finite on (0, R), so g(ρ) → L := inf g ∈ [0, ∞) as ρ ↓ 0, and ρ^{−n}μ(B_ρ(y)) = e^{−Λρ}g(ρ) → L. With θ := L/ω_n ≥ 0 we get M_{B_ρ(y)}(T)/(ω_n·ofReal(ρ^n)) → ofReal θ as ρ ↓ 0, i.e. HasMassDensity T y θ. Limits in [0, ∞] are unique, so this θ is unique; call it Θ(y), and put Θ(y) := 0 for y ∉ U.
6. ((iii), upper semicontinuity; Simon 3.11.) Θ of step 5 satisfies HasMassDensity T y (Θ(y)) for y ∈ U. To see that Θ is upper semicontinuous on U, let y_j → y with y_j, y ∈ U, choose R > 0 with closedBall y (2R) ⊆ U and Λ for K := closedBall y (2R), and let ρ, η > 0 with ρ + η < R. For large j, |y_j − y| < η, so closedBall y_j R ⊆ K and, by step 5 and monotonicity at y_j, Θ(y_j) ≤ e^{Λρ}μ(B_ρ(y_j))/(ω_nρ^n) ≤ e^{Λρ}μ(B_{ρ+η}(y))/(ω_nρ^n). Hence limsup_j Θ(y_j) ≤ e^{Λρ}μ(closedBall y (ρ + η))/(ω_nρ^n); letting η ↓ 0 replaces closedBall y (ρ + η) by closedBall y ρ, and letting ρ ↓ 0 gives limsup_j Θ(y_j) ≤ Θ(y), because (ω_nρ^n)^{−1}μ(closedBall y ρ) → Θ(y) as well (for s < ρ < s', μ(B_ρ(y)) ≤ μ(closedBall y ρ) ≤ μ(B_{s'}(y))).
7. ((iv).) For H^n-a.e. x ∈ M, Θ^n(μ, x) = θ(x) (Simon Ch. 3, Theorem 1.9 together with Ch. 4, Remark 1.8(2), as used at chapter-04.txt line 350: H^n⌞M has density 1 at H^n-a.e. point of the countably n-rectifiable set M, and H^n⌞M-a.e. point of M is a Lebesgue point of the locally integrable θ); since θ ≥ 1 on M, Θ ≥ 1 μ-a.e. Let y ∈ spt T and HasMassDensity T y θ_y; by uniqueness θ_y = Θ(y). By im_mass_measure (b), μ(B_ε(y)) > 0 for every ε > 0, so every small ball B_ε(y) ⊆ U contains a point z_ε with Θ(z_ε) ≥ 1. By step 6, θ_y = Θ(y) ≥ limsup_{ε↓0} Θ(z_ε) ≥ 1.

subproblems.title: Near a regular point the density is a constant positive integer on the support
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, let T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and let y ∈ reg T (regularSet T, Simon 7.4.1 as in the contract: y ∈ spt T and for some ρ₀ > 0 with B_{ρ₀}(y) ⊆ U, some m₀ ∈ ℤ ∖ {0} and some embedded C¹ n-dimensional submanifold M ∋ y with a continuous orientation ξ (IsOrientation) and H^n(M ∩ K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ B_{ρ₀}(y), T(ω) = m₀∫_M ξ(x)(ω(x)) dH^n(x) for all ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ B_{ρ₀}(y)). Then there are m ∈ ℕ with m ≥ 1 and ρ > 0 such that HasMassDensity T z m (Θ^n(μ_T, z) = m) for every z ∈ spt T ∩ B_ρ(y).

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the regularity facts "x ∈ reg T, T = m[[M]] near x, μ_T = |m|H^n⌞M, hence Θ^n(μ_T, x) = |m|" used in the parent proof (steps B2, C4, C5, G(c)); the details are supplied. H^n := μHE[n]; |α| is the Euclidean coefficient norm of covectors (covectorEuclideanNorm); ω_n := unitBallVolume n.
1. (Data.) Unfold y ∈ regularSet T: y ∈ spt T, ρ₀ > 0 with B_{ρ₀}(y) ⊆ U, m₀ ∈ ℤ ∖ {0}, M with y ∈ M, IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 n M, ξ with IsOrientation n M ξ (ξ continuous on M and, for every x ∈ M, ξ(x)(α) = ±α(τ_1, …, τ_n) for an orthonormal basis τ of the tangent space T_xM), H^n(M ∩ K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ B_{ρ₀}(y), and T(ω) = m₀∫_M ξ(x)(ω(x)) dH^n for ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ B_{ρ₀}(y). Put m := |m₀| ∈ ℕ, so m ≥ 1.
2. (Local closedness.) Let (V, W, ψ) be the chart of M at y given by IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 n M: W is open with y ∈ W, ψ(V) = W ∩ M, ψ is C¹ and injective on the open set V ⊆ ℝ^n with injective differential, and V ∩ ψ^{−1}(K) is compact for every compact K ⊆ W. Choose ρ₁ ∈ (0, ρ₀/2) with closedBall y (2ρ₁) ⊆ W. Then M ∩ closedBall y (2ρ₁) = ψ(V ∩ ψ^{−1}(closedBall y (2ρ₁))) is compact, so M ∩ B_{2ρ₁}(y) is relatively closed in B_{2ρ₁}(y).
3. (Mass of T on small balls.) Let z ∈ ℝ^P and s > 0 with B_s(z) ⊆ B_{ρ₀}(y). Claim: M_{B_s(z)}(T) = m·H^n(M ∩ B_s(z)). (≤) For admissible ω (tsupport ω ⊆ B_s(z), |ω| ≤ 1), the pointwise duality |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for a unit simple orientation (Cauchy–Binet: α(τ_1, …, τ_n) = Σ_I α(e_I)det(τ^I) with Σ_I det(τ^I)² = 1) gives T(ω) ≤ m∫_{M∩B_s(z)} |ω| dH^n ≤ m·H^n(M ∩ B_s(z)). (≥) Let β(x) := sign(m₀)·Σ_I ξ(x)(dx^I)dx^I for x ∈ M; β is continuous on M, |β| = 1 and m₀·ξ(x)(β(x)) = m. Let K ⊆ M ∩ B_s(z) be compact and ε > 0; since H^n⌞M is finite on compact subsets of B_{ρ₀}(y) (outer regularity), choose an open V' with K ⊆ V', closure V' ⊆ B_s(z) compact and m·H^n(M ∩ V' ∖ K) < ε. Extend β|_K continuously to ℝ^P (Tietze, coordinatewise), compose with the retraction α ↦ α/max(1, |α|), multiply by χ ∈ C_c(V'; [0, 1]) with χ = 1 on K, and mollify: this gives smooth admissible forms ω_j (tsupport in V', |ω_j| ≤ 1) converging uniformly to a continuous γ with γ = β on K, |γ| ≤ 1 and γ = 0 off V'. By dominated convergence T(ω_j) → m₀∫_M ξ(γ) dH^n ≥ m·H^n(K) − m·H^n(M ∩ V' ∖ K) ≥ m·H^n(K) − ε. As K and ε are arbitrary, inner regularity of the finite measure H^n⌞(M ∩ B_s(z)) gives M_{B_s(z)}(T) ≥ m·H^n(M ∩ B_s(z)).
4. (Density of a C¹ submanifold.) Let z ∈ M ∩ B_{2ρ₁}(y). If n = 0, M is discrete near z (V ⊆ Euclid 0 is a point, so W ∩ M is a single point) and H^0(M ∩ B_s(z)) = 1 = ω_0s^0 for small s > 0 (μHE[0] is counting measure); assume n ≥ 1. Near z, M is the graph {z + v + u(v)} of a C¹ map u from a neighbourhood of 0 in the n-plane T_zM into (T_zM)^⊥ with u(0) = 0 and Du(0) = 0: write z = ψ(v_z) with v_z ∈ V; by properness and injectivity of ψ on V, points of M sufficiently close to z are images of points of V close to v_z (if ψ(v_j) → z then, V ∩ ψ^{−1}(closedBall z ε) being compact, every subsequence of (v_j) has a further subsequence converging to some v'' ∈ V with ψ(v'') = z, i.e. v'' = v_z), and by the inverse function theorem ψ maps a neighbourhood of v_z onto such a C¹ graph over T_zM = Dψ(v_z)(ℝ^n). By the area formula (μHE[n] restricted to an n-dimensional affine plane is its Lebesgue measure), H^n(M ∩ B_s(z)) = ∫_{G_s} J_u dL^n, where G_s := {v : |v|² + |u(v)|² < s²} and J_u(v) = (det(I + Du(v)ᵀDu(v)))^{1/2} → 1 as v → 0. Since |u(v)| = o(|v|), (T_zM ∩ B_{s(1−o(1))}(0)) ⊆ G_s ⊆ T_zM ∩ B_s(0), so H^n(M ∩ B_s(z)) = ω_n s^n(1 + o(1)) as s ↓ 0.
5. (Conclusion.) Put ρ := ρ₁. Let z ∈ spt T ∩ B_ρ(y). First, z ∈ M: otherwise, since M ∩ closedBall y (2ρ₁) is compact and z ∈ B_{ρ₁}(y), there is s ∈ (0, ρ₁) with B_s(z) ∩ M = ∅, and then T(ω) = m₀∫_M ξ(ω) dH^n = 0 for all ω with tsupport ω ⊆ B_s(z); since closure B_s(z) is a compact subset of B_{ρ₀}(y) ⊆ U, z would lie in zeroRegion(T), contradicting z ∈ spt T. So z ∈ M ∩ B_{ρ₁}(y). For 0 < s < ρ₀/2 we have B_s(z) ⊆ B_{ρ₀}(y), so by steps 3 and 4, M_{B_s(z)}(T)/(ω_n s^n) = m·H^n(M ∩ B_s(z))/(ω_n s^n) → m as s ↓ 0. Since m ≥ 0, this is HasMassDensity T z m.
proof_key_steps: Unfold regularSet: T = m₀[[M]] on B_{ρ₀}(y) with M an embedded C¹ n-submanifold through y and m := |m₀| ≥ 1.
M is relatively closed near y, so spt T ∩ B_ρ(y) ⊆ M for small ρ.
M_{B_s(z)}(T) = m·H^n(M ∩ B_s(z)) by the duality |ξ(α)| ≤ |α| and smooth approximation of the dual covector field of ξ.
A C¹ embedded submanifold has H^n-density 1 at each of its points (graph and area formula), so Θ^n(μ_T, z) = m on spt T ∩ B_ρ(y).

subproblems.title: Blow-up compactness with moving centres (Simon Remark 7.2.5(2))
subproblems.statement: Let n, k, ℓ ∈ ℕ with 1 ≤ n and ℓ ≤ k, let U ⊆ ℝ^{n+k} be open, let N be an embedded C² (n+ℓ)-dimensional submanifold of ℝ^{n+k} with (closure N ∖ N) ∩ U = ∅, and let T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) be minimizing in U ∩ N with spt T ⊆ U ∩ N and ∂T = 0 in U. Let x ∈ U, let x_j → x be points of ℝ^{n+k} and let λ_j > 0 with λ_j → 0. Then there are a strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ and C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^{n+k}) such that the blow-ups S_j := η_{x_{φ(j)},λ_{φ(j)}#}T (blowUp T x_{φ(j)} λ_{φ(j)}, currents in η_{x_{φ(j)},λ_{φ(j)}}(U), η_{a,λ}(w) = λ^{−1}(w − a)) converge weakly to C in ℝ^{n+k} (ConvergesWeakly), μ_{S_j} → μ_C as Radon measures on ℝ^{n+k} for all integer multiplicity representations (MassMeasuresConverge), C is minimizing in ℝ^{n+k} (IsMinimizingIn C univ) and ∂C = 0.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent step T2 (Simon Remark 7.2.5(2), chapter-07.txt lines 166–174, "left to the reader"), obtained by running the proof of Simon 7.2.4 (book lines 176–288) with retractions onto the rescaled submanifolds. P := n + k. For an integer multiplicity current S, μ_S denotes R.measure for any representation R; by the sibling child im_mass_measure all representations of S have the same measure (part (c)), it equals M_W(S) on open W (part (a)), and spt S = spt μ_S inside the domain (part (b)).
1. (Scaling.) Write η_j := η_{x_j,λ_j} and S_j := η_{j#}T ∈ 𝒟_n(η_j(U)) (we rename subsequences freely). By the definition of blowUp (affine push-forward of T restricted along η_j^{−1}(η_j(U)) = U), S_j(ω) = T(η_j^#ω) with η_j^#ω(w) = λ_j^{−n}ω(η_j(w)) because Dη_j = λ_j^{−1}I. Hence: (a) M_W(S_j) = λ_j^{−n}M_{η_j^{−1}(W)}(T) for open W ⊆ η_j(U), and S_j is integer multiplicity, represented by (η_j(M), θ∘η_j^{−1}, ξ∘η_j^{−1}) if (M, θ, ξ) represents T (H^n(η_j(A)) = λ_j^{−n}H^n(A); dilations preserve approximate tangent planes and their orientations), so μ_{S_j} = λ_j^{−n}(η_j)_#μ_T; (b) ∂S_j = η_{j#}∂T = 0 (boundary commutes with affine push-forward, SimonGMT GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_affinePushforward); (c) S_j is minimizing in η_j(U) ∩ η_j(N): a competitor S' of S_j in an open W ⊂⊂ η_j(U) is the push-forward by η_j of the competitor η_j^{−1}#S' of T in η_j^{−1}(W) (integer multiplicity, boundaries, compact containment and supports correspond, and masses scale by the same factor λ_j^{−n}); (d) spt S_j = η_j(spt T) ⊆ η_j(N); (e) currentEval(S_j, ω) = S_j(ω) whenever tsupport ω ⊆ η_j(U).
2. (Uniform mass bounds.) Choose δ > 0 with closedBall x (2δ) ⊆ U and let Λ ≥ 0 be given by the sibling child monotonicity (i) (with P = n + k, d := n + ℓ) for K := closedBall x (2δ). For j with |x_j − x| < δ we have closedBall x_j δ ⊆ K, so for 0 < ρ < δ/2, e^{Λρ}ρ^{−n}μ_T(B_ρ(x_j)) ≤ e^{Λδ/2}(δ/2)^{−n}μ_T(B_{δ/2}(x_j)) ≤ c₁ := e^{Λδ}(2/δ)^nμ_T(K) < ∞. Hence for every R > 0 and all large j (|x_j − x| < δ and λ_jR < δ/2): M_{B_R(0)}(S_j) = λ_j^{−n}μ_T(B_{λ_jR}(x_j)) ≤ c₁R^n, and B_R(0) ⊆ η_j(B_δ(x_j)) ⊆ η_j(U).
3. (Weak limit.) By the weak compactness lemma for currents with locally bounded mass (Simon Ch. 6, 2.15), applied on the balls B_R(0), R ∈ ℕ, together with a diagonal argument, there are a subsequence and C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with currentEval(S_j, ω) → C(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P) (each ω has support in some B_R(0), on which the S_j are eventually defined with M_{B_R(0)}(S_j) ≤ c₁R^n). Since ∂S_j = 0 on B_R(0) for large j, C(dω) = lim S_j(dω) = 0, i.e. ∂C = 0 (n ≥ 1). By the Federer–Fleming compactness theorem (Simon Ch. 6, 3.11), applied on each B_R(0) to the integer multiplicity S_j with bounded M_{B_R(0)}(S_j) and ∂S_j = 0, C is integer multiplicity.
4. (Case A: dist(x_j, N)/λ_j unbounded.) Pass to a subsequence with dist(x_j, N)/λ_j → ∞. For each R, B_R(0) ∩ η_j(N) = ∅ for large j (a point w of the intersection would give x_j + λ_jw ∈ N at distance < λ_jR from x_j). By 1(d), S_j vanishes on B_R(0) for large j, so C = 0 and μ_{S_j}(B_R(0)) = 0 eventually; hence μ_{S_j} → 0 = μ_C, C = 0 is integer multiplicity (empty representation) and minimizing (M_W(0) = 0 ≤ M_W(S')), ∂C = 0, and the theorem holds. Otherwise:
5. (Case B: dist(x_j, N) ≤ C₀λ_j for all j and some C₀ ≥ 1.) Then x ∈ closure(N) ∩ U ⊆ N. Since N is an embedded C² submanifold, there is δ₁ ∈ (0, δ) such that the nearest-point projection π onto N is well defined and C¹ on B_{δ₁}(x), maps B_{δ₁}(x) into N, is the identity on N ∩ B_{δ₁}(x), and satisfies |Dπ(w')| ≤ 1 + c·dist(w', N) for w' ∈ B_{δ₁}(x) (tubular neighbourhood theorem; c bounds the second fundamental form of N near x); hence Lip(π|B_s(w)) ≤ 1 + cs for w ∈ N ∩ B_{δ₁/2}(x) and s < δ₁/2. Fix R > 0. For large j, π_j := η_j∘π∘η_j^{−1} is defined and C¹ on η_j(B_{δ₁}(x)) ⊇ B_R(0), maps into η_j(N), is the identity on η_j(N) ∩ B_R(0), satisfies |π_j(w) − w| = dist(w, η_j(N)) ≤ |w| + dist(0, η_j(N)) ≤ |w| + C₀, and L_j := Lip(π_j|B_R(0)) ≤ 1 + cλ_j(R + C₀) → 1 (B_R(0) = η_j(B_{λ_jR}(x_j)) ⊆ η_j(B_{λ_j(R+C₀)}(w_j)) for a nearest point w_j ∈ N of x_j).
6. (Comparison; Simon 7.2.4, book (1)–(11).) Fix a compact K ⊆ ℝ^P and ε > 0; take ψ ∈ C^∞_c(ℝ^P; [0, 1]) with ψ = 1 near K and spt ψ ⊆ {dist(·, K) < ε}, and G > 0 with spt ψ ⊆ B_G(0) and |w| + C₀ < G/2 for w ∈ spt ψ; apply step 5 with some R > G, and put W_s := {ψ > s}. (a) By Simon Ch. 6, 7.2 (weak convergence with locally bounded masses of S_j and ∂S_j implies flat convergence), C − S_j = ∂R_j + S'_j in W_0 with R_j, S'_j integer multiplicity and M_{W_0}(R_j) + M_{W_0}(S'_j) → 0. (b) By slicing (Ch. 6, 4.5) choose α ∈ (0, 1) and a subsequence with ∂(R_j⌞W_α) = (∂R_j)⌞W_α + P_j, P_j integer multiplicity, spt P_j ⊆ ∂W_α, M(P_j) → 0, and with μ_{S_j}(∂W_α) = 0 for all j and μ_C(∂W_α) = 0. Then C⌞W_α = S_j⌞W_α + ∂R̃_j + S̃_j with R̃_j := R_j⌞W_α, S̃_j := S'_j⌞W_α − P_j, M(R̃_j) + M(S̃_j) → 0. (c) Let X be an integer multiplicity cycle with spt X ⊆ K. Put Y_j := X + ∂R̃_j (an integer multiplicity cycle with spt Y_j ⊆ closure W_α ⊆ spt ψ) and Z_j := S_j + π_{j#}Y_j, where π_{j#} is applied only to the compactly supported Y_j (Simon Ch. 6, 2.23 and 3.3–3.9: the push-forward of a compactly supported integer multiplicity current by a C¹ map is integer multiplicity). Then ∂Z_j = ∂S_j + π_{j#}∂Y_j = 0 = ∂S_j, and spt(Z_j − S_j) ⊆ π_j(spt Y_j) is a compact subset of η_j(N) ∩ B_G(0) (|π_j(w)| ≤ 2|w| + C₀ < G for w ∈ spt ψ); for large j, closure B_G(0) ⊆ η_j(U). By 1(c), M_{B_G(0)}(S_j) ≤ M_{B_G(0)}(Z_j). (d) π_j is C¹ and the identity on η_j(N) ∩ B_R(0) ⊇ spt S_j ∩ B_R(0); the approximate tangent planes of S_j are μ_{S_j}-a.e. contained in the tangent planes of η_j(N), on which Dπ_j is the identity; so the push-forward formula for integer multiplicity currents (Ch. 6, 2.24(2), 3.3–3.9) gives π_{j#}(S_j⌞B_G(0)) = S_j⌞B_G(0). Hence Z_j⌞B_G(0) = π_{j#}((S_j + Y_j)⌞B_G(0)) and μ_{S_j}(B_G(0)) ≤ μ_{Z_j}(B_G(0)) ≤ L_j^n μ_{S_j+Y_j}(B_G(0)). (e) S_j + Y_j = S_j outside closure W_α, the part of Y_j on ∂W_α is P_j, and μ_{S_j}(∂W_α) = 0, so the last inequality gives μ_{S_j}(W_α) ≤ μ_{S_j+Y_j}(W_α) + L_j^nM(P_j) + (L_j^n − 1)Λ_G with Λ_G := sup_j(μ_{S_j+Y_j}(B_G(0)) + μ_{S_j}(B_G(0))) ≤ 2c₁G^n + M(X) + sup_j M(∂R̃_j) < ∞ (∂R̃_j = (C − S_j)⌞W_α − S̃_j). Since (S_j + Y_j)⌞W_α = (C + X − S̃_j)⌞W_α by (b), M_{W_α}(S_j) ≤ M_{W_α}(C + X) + ε_j with ε_j := M(S̃_j) + L_j^nM(P_j) + (L_j^n − 1)Λ_G → 0.
7. (Minimality of C.) By lower semicontinuity of mass under weak convergence on the open set W_α (SimonGMT WeaklyConvergesOn.massOn_le_liminf, applied to the restrictions to B_R(0)), M_{W_α}(C) ≤ liminf_j M_{W_α}(S_j) ≤ M_{W_α}(C + X). Now let W ⊂⊂ ℝ^P be open and S' integer multiplicity with ∂S' = ∂C = 0 and spt(S' − C) compact ⊆ W. Apply the above with X := S' − C (integer multiplicity by Ch. 6, 3.2(1), a cycle), K := spt X and ε < dist(K, ℝ^P ∖ W), so W_α ⊆ W. Since S' = C off K (μ_{S'} = μ_C on the open set ℝ^P ∖ K), M_W(C) = μ_C(W_α) + μ_C(W ∖ W_α) ≤ μ_{S'}(W_α) + μ_{S'}(W ∖ W_α) = M_W(S') (im_mass_measure). C is integer multiplicity (step 3), so IsMinimizingIn C univ.
8. (Measure convergence.) With X = 0, step 6(e) gives limsup_j μ_{S_j}(K) ≤ limsup_j μ_{S_j}(W_α) ≤ μ_C(W_α) ≤ μ_C({dist(·, K) < ε}); letting ε ↓ 0, limsup_j μ_{S_j}(K) ≤ μ_C(K). Fix a countable family {ω_m} ⊆ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P) such that for every R ∈ ℕ, every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P) with tsupport ω ⊆ B_R(0) and every ε > 0 there is m with tsupport ω_m ⊆ B_{R+1}(0) and sup_w |ω(w) − ω_m(w)| < ε (|·| the Euclidean coefficient norm); for instance the forms χ_R·Σ_I p_I dx^I (R ∈ ℕ, I increasing multi-indices) with a fixed χ_R ∈ C^∞_c(B_{R+1}(0); [0, 1]) equal to 1 on closedBall 0 R and polynomials p_I with rational coefficients: approximate the coefficients of ω uniformly on closedBall 0 (R + 1) by such p_I (Weierstrass); since ω = 0 off B_R(0) and χ_R = 1 on closedBall 0 R, sup|ω − χ_R·p| ≤ sup_{closedBall 0 (R+1)}|ω − p|. Criterion (C): let V_k ⊆ ℝ^P be open, A_k ∈ 𝒟_n(V_k) and A ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P), and suppose that for every R ∈ ℕ there are k_R ∈ ℕ and Γ_R < ∞ with B_{R+1}(0) ⊆ V_k and M_{B_{R+1}(0)}(A_k) ≤ Γ_R for all k ≥ k_R, and M_{B_{R+1}(0)}(A) ≤ Γ_R. If A_k(ω_m) → A(ω_m) for every m (for k ≥ k_R these values are defined when tsupport ω_m ⊆ B_{R+1}(0)), then currentEval(A_k, ω) → A(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P), i.e. A_k ⇀ A in ℝ^P (ConvergesWeakly). Proof: let tsupport ω ⊆ B_R(0) and ε > 0, and choose ω_m as above. For k ≥ k_R, tsupport ω ⊆ V_k, so currentEval(A_k, ω) = A_k(ω); a test form β with tsupport β ⊆ W (W open) and sup|β| ≤ s satisfies |A'(β)| ≤ s·M_W(A') for every current A' (if s > 0, ±β/s is admissible for M_W(A')), so |A_k(ω) − A_k(ω_m)| ≤ Γ_Rε and |A(ω) − A(ω_m)| ≤ Γ_Rε; hence limsup_k |currentEval(A_k, ω) − A(ω)| ≤ 2Γ_Rε for every ε > 0. (The criterion is used only for limits on all of ℝ^P approximated by currents whose domains exhaust ℝ^P, and no metric for weak convergence on varying bounded domains is used: for a limit on a bounded domain, currentEval vanishes at the limit on a form whose support meets the boundary of the limit domain, although it need not vanish along the approximants. For example, in ℝ (n = P = 1) let λ_i ↑ 1, A_i := [[(−2/λ_i, 2/λ_i)]] ∈ 𝒟_1((−2/λ_i, 2/λ_i)) and A := [[(−2, 2)]] ∈ 𝒟_1((−2, 2)): A_i ⇀ A in (−2, 2) and μ_{A_i} → μ_A vaguely there, but for ω = g dx with spt g = [−2, 2] and ∫g > 0, currentEval(A_i, ω) = ∫g > 0 for every i while currentEval(A, ω) = 0.) (e) (Tangent cones of members.) Let (S, U_S) ∈ 𝒯 have parameters (x, λ), |y| < 1 and λ_k ↓ 0. Case λ > 0. Since η_{y,λ_k}∘η_{x,λ} = η_{x+λy,λλ_k}, η_{y,λ_k#}S = η_{x+λy,λλ_k#}T'; these are the restrictions to η_{x+λy,λλ_k}(B_2(0)) of the blow-ups blowUp T (z + r(x + λy)) (rλλ_k) of T at z + r(x + λy) ∈ B_r(z) (|x + λy| < 1 − λ + λ = 1) with scales rλλ_k → 0, and their domains η_{x+λy,λλ_k}(B_2(0)) ⊇ B_{(2−|x+λy|)/(λλ_k)}(0) exhaust ℝ^P. If z + r(x + λy) ∈ spt T, the sibling density_and_tangent_cones (2) (boundarySupport T = ∅) gives a strictly increasing subsequence along which these blow-ups converge weakly in ℝ^P (ConvergesWeakly), with convergence of the mass measures (MassMeasuresConverge), to a minimizing cone C; otherwise T vanishes on a ball around z + r(x + λy), the blow-ups vanish on every ball B_R(0) for large k, and C := 0. Because every compact set eventually lies in η_{x+λy,λλ_k}(B_2(0)), on which η_{y,λ_k#}S agrees with the blow-up of T, η_{y,λ_k#}S ⇀ C in ℝ^P and μ_{η_{y,λ_k#}S} → μ_C vaguely on ℝ^P along the subsequence; and C is a member with parameters (x + λy, 0) via the sequence x'_k := x + λy, λ'_k := λλ_k (k so large that λλ_k < 1 − |x + λy|): for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P), tsupport ω ⊆ η_{x'_k,λ'_k}(B_2(0)) for large k and (η_{x'_k,λ'_k#}T')(ω) = currentEval(blowUp T (z + r(x + λy)) (rλλ_k), ω) → C(ω). Case λ = 0. By (b), S is integer multiplicity and minimizing in ℝ^P with ∂S = 0. If y ∈ spt S, the sibling density_and_tangent_cones (2) (U = N = ℝ^P, ℓ := k, the codimension P − n) gives a strictly increasing subsequence along which η_{y,λ_k#}S ⇀ C in ℝ^P and μ_{η_{y,λ_k#}S} → μ_C vaguely, C a minimizing cone; if y ∉ spt S, η_{y,λ_k#}S vanishes on every B_R(0) for large k and C := 0. Diagonal selection: pass to that subsequence, discard the k with λ_k ≥ 1 − |y|, and let (x_i, s_i) be a defining sequence of S (x_i → x, s_i ∈ (0, 1), s_i → 0, |x_i| < 1 − s_i, and η_{x_i,s_i#}T' → S in the sense of the definition of 𝒯; the letter s_i is used to distinguish these scales from the tangent scales λ_k). For each k and i put A_{k,i} := η_{x_i+s_iy,s_iλ_k#}T', a current on η_{x_i+s_iy,s_iλ_k}(B_2(0)). As η_{y,λ_k}∘η_{x_i,s_i} = η_{x_i+s_iy,s_iλ_k}, A_{k,i}(ω) = (η_{x_i,s_i#}T')(η_{y,λ_k}^#ω) whenever tsupport ω lies in the domain of A_{k,i}; since η_{y,λ_k}^#ω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P), the defining property of S gives, for fixed k and ω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P): tsupport ω lies in the domain of A_{k,i} for all large i, and A_{k,i}(ω) → S(η_{y,λ_k}^#ω) = (η_{y,λ_k#}S)(ω) as i → ∞. Choose i(1) < i(2) < ⋯ with s_{i(k)} < 1/k, |x_{i(k)} − x| < 1/k, and, for all m ≤ k, tsupport ω_m inside the domain of A_{k,i(k)} and |A_{k,i(k)}(ω_m) − (η_{y,λ_k#}S)(ω_m)| < 1/k (finitely many conditions, each holding for all large i). Put D_k := A_{k,i(k)}, x'_k := x_{i(k)} + s_{i(k)}y and λ'_k := s_{i(k)}λ_k. Then λ'_k ∈ (0, 1), λ'_k → 0, x'_k → x, and |x'_k| < 1 − s_{i(k)} + s_{i(k)}|y| ≤ 1 − s_{i(k)}λ_k = 1 − λ'_k (as |y| ≤ 1 − λ_k). Eventual support containment: the domain of D_k is η_{x'_k,λ'_k}(B_2(0)) = B_{2/λ'_k}(−x'_k/λ'_k) ⊇ B_{1/λ'_k}(0) because |x'_k| < 1, so every compact subset of ℝ^P lies in the domain of D_k for all large k. Mass bounds: by (d), M_{B_{R+1}(0)}(D_k) ≤ c₂(R + 1)^n as soon as B_{R+1}(0) lies in the domain of D_k, and M_{B_{R+1}(0)}(C) ≤ liminf_k M_{B_{R+1}(0)}(η_{y,λ_k#}S) ≤ c₂(R + 1)^n by lower semicontinuity of mass, η_{y,λ_k#}S being a member by (c) (0 < λ_k < 1, |y| ≤ 1 − λ_k). Tests: for each m and all k ≥ m, |D_k(ω_m) − C(ω_m)| < 1/k + |(η_{y,λ_k#}S)(ω_m) − C(ω_m)| → 0. By criterion (C) of (d), D_k ⇀ C in ℝ^P, i.e. for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P), tsupport ω ⊆ η_{x'_k,λ'_k}(B_2(0)) for large k and (η_{x'_k,λ'_k#}T')(ω) → C(ω): C is a member with parameters (x, 0) = (x + λy, 0). In both cases, along the chosen strictly increasing subsequence, μ_{η_{y,λ_k#}S} → μ_C vaguely on ℝ^P and C is a cone. (f) A member with μ_S ≠ 0 and μ_S(λA) = λ^nμ_S(A) for all λ > 0, or with μ_S(ℝ^P) = ∞, has parameter λ = 0 (members with λ > 0 have finite positive total mass, which a nonzero n-homogeneous measure cannot have).
3. (Density functions; parent T5.) Let e₁ be the unit vector of Euclid 1, H^n := μHE[n], and c_n := addHaarScalarFactor(volume, μH[n]) ∈ ℝ≥0 (the scalar in Mathlib's definition μHE[n] = c_n·μH[n]); c_n ≠ 0 (addHaarScalarFactor_volume_hausdorffMeasure_ne_zero), so c_n ∈ (0, ∞) and H^n = c_n·μH[n]. Consider integer multiplicity currents A on open sets V_A ⊆ ℝ^P whose mass measure μ_A, extended by 0 outside V_A, is locally finite on ℝ^P; these include all members (finite total mass if λ > 0, μ_S(B_R(0)) ≤ c₂R^n if λ = 0, by 2(d)), all their rescalings η_{y,λ#}S, and the cones C of 2(e). For such A put ϑ_A(w) := limsup_{ρ↓0} μ_A(B_ρ(w))/(ω_nρ^n) when finite and 0 otherwise, and φ_A(w) := ϑ_A(w)·e₁; write ϑ_S, φ_S for members. Then: (i) ϑ_S = Θ_S on U_S (densities exist there by 2(a), 2(b)). (ii) ϑ_A is Borel. (iii) μ_A = ϑ_A·H^n as measures on ℝ^P (Θ^n(μ_A, ·) equals the multiplicity H^n-a.e. on the carrier by Simon Ch. 3, Theorem 1.9 and Ch. 4, Remark 1.8(2), and the upper density vanishes H^n-a.e. off the carrier by Simon Ch. 1, Theorem 3.6 with Remark 3.7(2), applied to the locally finite measure μ_A on ℝ^P). (iv) (Normalization.) Since H^n = c_n·μH[n], (iii) gives μ_A = c_n·ϑ_A·μH[n], i.e. ∫ g·ϑ_A dμH[n] = c_n^{−1}·∫ g dμ_A for every bounded Borel g with compact support; in particular ∫_K ϑ_A dμH[n] = c_n^{−1}·μ_A(K) < ∞ for every compact K, so φ_A (Borel, ‖φ_A‖ = ϑ_A) is locally μH[n]-integrable. (H0) holds for members: if φ_S = φ_{S'} μH[n]-a.e., then ϑ_S = ϑ_{S'} H^n-a.e. (e₁ ≠ 0) (H^n and μH[n] have the same null sets), so μ_S = μ_{S'} by (iii), hence ϑ_S = ϑ_{S'} everywhere (ϑ is computed from μ) and φ_S = φ_{S'}. (v) (Correctly normalized weak pairings.) For every continuous compactly supported f : ℝ^P → ℝ, ∫ f·φ_A dμH[n] = (∫ f·ϑ_A dμH[n])·e₁ = c_n^{−1}(∫ f dμ_A)·e₁. Hence, for currents A_k, A as above, φ_{A_k} ⇀ φ_A in the sense of the sibling abstract_dimension_reduction (∫ f·φ_{A_k} dμH[n] → ∫ f·φ_A dμH[n] for all such f) if and only if ∫ f dμ_{A_k} → ∫ f dμ_A for all such f, i.e. μ_{A_k} → μ_A vaguely on ℝ^P (the factor c_n^{−1} ∈ (0, ∞) and the vector e₁ are fixed). (vi) φ_{η_{y,λ#}A}(w) = φ_A(y + λw) for all w (μ_{η_{y,λ#}A} = λ^{−n}(η_{y,λ})_#μ_A, so μ_{η_{y,λ#}A}(B_ρ(w)) = λ^{−n}μ_A(B_{λρ}(y + λw))). 4. (Semicontinuity along members; parent T3.) Let (S_k, U_{S_k}), (S, U_S) ∈ 𝒯 with μ_{S_k} → μ_S vaguely on ℝ^P, and w_k → w with |w| ≤ 1. Then Θ_S(w) ≥ limsup_k Θ_{S_k}(w_k). Indeed B_2(0) ⊆ U_{S_k} ∩ U_S, and all members satisfy the monotonicity of 2(a)/(b) with the common constant Λ₀ on balls inside closedBall 0 2. For ρ, η > 0 with ρ + η < 1/2 and large k (|w_k − w| < η): Θ_{S_k}(w_k) ≤ e^{Λ₀ρ}μ_{S_k}(B_ρ(w_k))/(ω_nρ^n) ≤ e^{Λ₀ρ}μ_{S_k}(closedBall w (ρ + η))/(ω_nρ^n), and limsup_k μ_{S_k}(closedBall w (ρ + η)) ≤ μ_S(closedBall w (ρ + η)) (vague convergence, compact set); let η ↓ 0 and then ρ ↓ 0.
5. (The threshold map; parent T9.) For any φ : ℝ^P → Euclid 1 put sing φ := closure{w : ⟨φ(w), e₁⟩ ≥ c}. (α) sing φ is closed. (β) A.3(2) holds exactly for every φ: sing(φ(y + λ·)) = {w : y + λw ∈ sing φ}, since w ↦ y + λw is a homeomorphism. (γ) For members, {w ∈ U_S : Θ_S(w) ≥ c} is relatively closed in U_S (upper semicontinuity of Θ_S on U_S: for λ > 0 inherited from Θ_T, for λ = 0 from 2(b)) and U_S is open, so sing φ_S ∩ U_S = {w ∈ U_S : Θ_S(w) ≥ c}; for parameter-0 members sing φ_S = {w : Θ_S(w) ≥ c}. (δ) A.3(1): let φ_S ∈ F with φ_S = 1_Q·c'' for an n-dimensional subspace Q and c'' ∈ Euclid 1; write c' := ⟨c'', e₁⟩, so φ_S takes the values c'e₁ on Q and 0 off Q. If c' < c, then {⟨φ_S, e₁⟩ ≥ c} = ∅ (c > 0), so sing φ_S = ∅. If c' ≥ c > 0, then ϑ_S = c'·1_Q and μ_S = c'H^n⌞Q by 3(iii), which has infinite total mass; by 2(f) S has parameter 0, so by 2(b) S is an admissible zero-scale limit (with centres z + rx_i ∈ B_r(z), scales rλ_i → 0), minimizing in ℝ^P with ∂S = 0, and by 3(i) HasMassDensity S y (1_Q(y)·c') for every y; this contradicts (H1). So sing φ = ∅ for every such φ ∈ F. (ε) A.3(3): let φ_{S_k} ⇀ φ_S in F (so μ_{S_k} → μ_S vaguely by 3(v)) and ε > 0, and suppose that for infinitely many k there is w_k ∈ B_1(0) ∩ sing φ_{S_k} with dist(w_k, sing φ_S) ≥ ε. As B_1(0) ⊆ B_2(0) ⊆ U_{S_k}, (γ) gives Θ_{S_k}(w_k) ≥ c. Passing to a subsequence, w_k → w with |w| ≤ 1, and step 4 gives Θ_S(w) ≥ c, so w ∈ sing φ_S by (γ) (w ∈ B_2(0) ⊆ U_S), contradicting dist(w_k, sing φ_S) ≥ ε for large k. Hence for large k, B_1(0) ∩ sing φ_{S_k} ⊆ {x : ∃ z' ∈ sing φ_S, dist(x, z') < ε}.

So either (I) B_1(0) ∩ sing φ = ∅ for every φ ∈ F, or (II) there is d ∈ ℕ with d + 1 ≤ n such that μH[d + α](sing φ ∩ B_1(0)) = 0 for all φ ∈ F and α > 0, there are ψ ∈ F and a linear subspace L with dim L = d, sing ψ = L and ψ(y + λx) = ψ(x) for all y ∈ L, λ > 0, x, and, if d = 0, sing φ ∩ B_σ(0) is finite for all φ ∈ F and σ < 1.

Since c > 0, sing 0 = ∅ ≠ L (0 ∈ L), so ψ ≠ 0 and μ_S ≠ 0; ψ is homogeneous (take y = 0), so by 3(iii) μ_S(λA) = λ^nμ_S(A), and by 2(f) S has parameter 0. By 2(b), S is an admissible zero-scale limit: S is the ConvergesWeakly-limit of blowUp T (z + rx_i) (rλ_i) with z + rx_i ∈ B_r(z), rλ_i → 0, and S is minimizing in ℝ^P with ∂S = 0. By 3(i), ϑ_S = Θ_S everywhere, so the invariance of ψ gives: HasMassDensity S w θ implies HasMassDensity S (y + λw) θ for y ∈ L, λ > 0 (Θ_S exists everywhere and Θ_S(y + λw) = Θ_S(w)); and by 5(γ), {y : Θ_S(y) ≥ c} = sing ψ = L. Moreover d₀ ≤ d = dim L < n. This contradicts (H2). Hence in case (II), d ≤ d₀ − 1 (in particular d₀ ≥ 1).

By 5(γ) and the scaling of densities, sing φ_{T'} ∩ B_1(0) = {w ∈ B_1(0) : Θ_{T'}(w) ≥ c} = {w : z + rw ∈ Z(r)}, i.e. Z(r) = z + r·(sing φ_{T'} ∩ B_1(0)) (for x ∈ B_r(z), ∃θ ≥ c with HasMassDensity T x θ iff Θ_T(x) ≥ c, as densities exist and are unique). In case (I), Z(r) = ∅, and all three conclusions hold (μH[s](∅) = 0 for every real s). In case (II), d ≤ d₀ − 1 by step 7; for α > 0, s := d₀ − 1 + α = d + α' with α' := d₀ − 1 − d + α > 0, so μH[s](sing φ_{T'} ∩ B_1(0)) = 0 and, since w ↦ z + rw is a similarity with ratio r and s > 0, μH[s](Z(r)) = r^s·0 = 0. If d₀ = 0, case (II) is impossible (d ≤ −1), so Z(r) = ∅. If d₀ = 1 then, in case (II), d = 0 and sing φ_{T'} ∩ B_{1/2}(0) is finite, so Z(r/2) = z + r·(sing φ_{T'} ∩ B_{1/2}(0)) is finite; in case (I), Z(r/2) = ∅.
proof_key_steps: Rescale to T' = (η_{z,r#}T)⌞B_2(0) and form Simon's class 𝒯 of limits of η_{x_i,λ_i#}T'; parameter-0 members are admissible zero-scale limits of blow-ups of T (via moving_blowups), minimizing with ∂ = 0.

Scalar density functions φ_S = ϑ_S·e₁ with the correct normalization μ_S = c_n·ϑ_S·μH[n] (H^n = μHE[n] = c_n·μH[n]), so ∫_K ϑ_S dμH[n] = c_n⁻¹·μ_S(K) and weak convergence of the φ_S is vague convergence of the μ_S; they satisfy (H0), local integrability, A.1 and A.2 (tangent cones of members are members, via an explicit diagonal selection with a countable-test criterion for limits on ℝ^P with exhausting domains).
The threshold map sing φ = closure{⟨φ, e₁⟩ ≥ c} is closed, satisfies A.3(2) exactly, A.3(1) by hypothesis (H1), and A.3(3) by upper semicontinuity of densities along members.

Appendix A.4 (sibling abstract_dimension_reduction) gives (I) or (II); in (II) the extremal ψ = φ_S is a homogeneous L-invariant parameter-0 member with {Θ_S ≥ c} = L, so hypothesis (H2) forces dim L < d₀.
Rescaling back gives μH[d₀ − 1 + α](Z(r)) = 0, Z(r) = ∅ if d₀ = 0, and finiteness of Z(r/2) if d₀ = 1.

For all n, k, ℓ ∈ ℕ with ℓ ≤ k, all sets U, N ⊆ ℝ^{n+k} and every T ∈ 𝒟_n(U): if U is open, N is an embedded C² (n+ℓ)-dimensional submanifold (IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 2 (n + ℓ) N), (closure N ∖ N) ∩ U = ∅, T is minimizing in U ∩ N, spt T ⊆ U ∩ N and ∂T = 0 in U (BoundaryVanishes T), then there exist sets E ⊆ F ⊆ ℝ^{n+k} such that μH[n − 3 + α](E) = 0 for every real α > 0; for every x ∈ U ∖ E there is an integer m with HasMassDensity T x m; μH[n − 2 + α](F) = 0 for every real α > 0; and HasTangentPlaneAt T x for every x ∈ spt T ∖ F.

Hence, for currents A_k, A as above, φ_{A_k} ⇀ φ_A in the sense of the sibling abstract_dimension_reduction (∫ f·φ_{A_k} dμH[n] → ∫ f·φ_A dμH[n] for all such f) if and only if ∫ f dμ_{A_k} → ∫ f dμ_A for all such f, i.e. μ_{A_k} → μ_A vaguely on ℝ^P (the factor c_n^{−1} ∈ (0, ∞) and the vector e₁ are fixed). (vi) φ_{η_{y,λ#}A}(w) = φ_A(y + λw) for all w (μ_{η_{y,λ#}A} = λ^{−n}(η_{y,λ})_#μ_A, so μ_{η_{y,λ#}A}(B_ρ(w)) = λ^{−n}μ_A(B_{λρ}(y + λw))). (vii) φ_C(λw) = φ_C(w) for cones C (μ_C(λB) = λ^nμ_C(B) for Borel B and λ > 0). So F := {φ_S : (S, U_S) ∈ 𝒯} satisfies (H0) and local integrability by (iv), A.1 by (c) and (vi), and A.2 of the sibling abstract_dimension_reduction: given φ_S ∈ F, |y| < 1 and a strictly decreasing sequence λ_k > 0 with λ_k → 0, (e) gives a strictly increasing subsequence k_i and a member cone C with μ_{η_{y,λ_{k_i}#}S} → μ_C vaguely on ℝ^P, so φ_S(y + λ_{k_i}·) = φ_{η_{y,λ_{k_i}#}S} ⇀ φ_C ∈ F by (vi) and (v), and φ_C is homogeneous by (vii). Two further facts, (viii) and (ix), and a consequence (T3s): (viii) (domain recovery) for φ with 0 < I(φ) := ∫|φ| dH^n < ∞ (H^n = μHE[n], so I(φ_S) = μ_S(ℝ^P) by (iii)) and ∫|w||φ(w)| dH^n(w) < ∞ put λ(φ) := (m₀/I(φ))^{1/n}, b(φ) := I(φ)^{−1}∫w|φ(w)| dH^n(w), x(φ) := b₀ − λ(φ)b(φ) and U(φ) := B_{2/λ(φ)}(−x(φ)/λ(φ)); otherwise U(φ) := ℝ^P. For members U(φ_S) = U_S (λ > 0: I(φ_S) = μ_S(ℝ^P) = λ^{−n}m₀ and b(φ_S) = (b₀ − x)/λ; λ = 0: I(φ_S) ∈ {0, ∞}), and U(φ_S(y + λ'·)) = η_{y,λ'}(U(φ_S)) by (c); (ix) (domain convergence) if μ_{S_k} → μ_S vaguely (members), every compact K ⊆ U_S lies in U_{S_k} for large k: otherwise, along a subsequence, λ_k > 0 and U_{S_k} ⊇ B_{1/λ_k}(0) force λ_k ≥ λ₀ > 0, the μ_{S_k} then live in closedBall 0 (3/λ₀) with total masses in [m₀, λ₀^{−n}m₀], so their total masses and barycenters converge, μ_S has finite positive mass, S has parameter λ > 0 by (b), (f), and (λ_k, x_k) → (λ, x), whence U_{S_k} → U_S and K ⊆ U_{S_k} for large k, a contradiction. (T3s) (parent T3, support part) If (S_k, U_{S_k}), (S, U_S) ∈ 𝒯 with μ_{S_k} → μ_S vaguely, y_k ∈ spt S_k and y_k → y ∈ U_S, then y ∈ spt S: choose ρ₁ > 0 with closedBall y (3ρ₁) ⊆ U_S; by (ix), closedBall y (3ρ₁) ⊆ U_{S_k} for large k, so (by (a), (b)) e^{Λ₀ρ}ρ^{−n}μ_{S_k}(B_ρ(y_k)) is nondecreasing on (0, ρ₁) for large k, and since Θ_{S_k}(y_k) ≥ 1, μ_{S_k}(B_ρ(y_k)) ≥ e^{−Λ₀ρ}ω_nρ^n for ρ < ρ₁; for η > 0 and large k, B_ρ(y_k) ⊆ closedBall y (ρ + η), so μ_S(closedBall y (ρ + η)) ≥ limsup_k μ_{S_k}(closedBall y (ρ + η)) ≥ e^{−Λ₀ρ}ω_nρ^n > 0 for all small ρ, η, i.e. y ∈ spt μ_S = spt S.
6. (A3: the flatness maps.) For j ≥ 1 put β_j := 2^{−j}. For any φ : ℝ^P → Euclid 1 let spt φ := {w : ∫_{B_ρ(w)}|φ| dμH[n] > 0 for all ρ > 0} (closed), R_j(φ) := {w ∈ spt φ : there are ρ > 0 and an n-dimensional subspace Π with B_ρ(w) ⊆ U(φ) and sup_{y ∈ spt φ ∩ B_ρ(w)}|q_Π(y − w)| < β_jρ} (q_Π the orthogonal projection onto Π^⊥, sup ∅ := 0), and sing_j φ := ((spt φ ∩ U(φ)) ∖ R_j(φ)) ∪ (ℝ^P ∖ U(φ)). For members, spt φ_S = spt μ_S and spt φ_S ∩ U_S = spt S. (Closed.) If (ρ, Π) witnesses w ∈ R_j(φ) with s := sup < β_jρ, and w' ∈ spt φ with t := |w' − w|, (1 + β_j)t < β_jρ − s, then (ρ − t, Π) witnesses w' (B_{ρ−t}(w') ⊆ B_ρ(w) and |q_Π(y − w')| ≤ s + t < β_j(ρ − t)); so R_j(φ) is relatively open in spt φ ∩ U(φ), (spt φ ∩ U(φ)) ∖ R_j(φ) is relatively closed in U(φ), and sing_j φ is closed. (A.3(2).) For members and g(w) := y + λ'w (0 < λ' < 1, |y| ≤ 1 − λ'): spt(φ∘g) = g^{−1}(spt φ), U(φ∘g) = g^{−1}(U(φ)) by (viii), and R_j(φ∘g) = g^{−1}(R_j(φ)) because balls and slabs scale together (B_ρ(w) ↦ B_{λ'ρ}(g(w)), |q_Π(g(y) − g(w))| = λ'|q_Π(y − w)|); hence sing_j(φ∘g) = g^{−1}(sing_j φ). (A.3(1).) If φ = c''·1_Q with Q an n-dimensional subspace: for c'' = 0, spt φ = ∅ and U(φ) = ℝ^P, so sing_j φ = ∅; for c'' ≠ 0, I(φ) = ∞, U(φ) = ℝ^P, spt φ = Q and every w ∈ Q is witnessed by (ρ, Π) = (1, Q) (sup = 0), so sing_j φ = ∅. (A.3(3).) Let φ_{S_k} ⇀ φ_S in F (so μ_{S_k} → μ_S vaguely), ε > 0, and suppose that along a subsequence w_k ∈ B_1(0) ∩ sing_j φ_{S_k} with dist(w_k, sing_j φ_S) ≥ ε. As B_2(0) ⊆ U_{S_k}, w_k ∈ spt S_k ∖ R_j(φ_{S_k}); pass to w_k → w, |w| ≤ 1; by (T3s), w ∈ spt S, and w ∉ sing_j φ_S (distance ≥ ε), w ∈ U_S, so w ∈ R_j(φ_S), witnessed by (ρ, Π) with s := sup_{y ∈ spt S ∩ B_ρ(w)}|q_Π(y − w)| < β_jρ. Take ρ' < ρ with s < β_jρ', τ := (s + β_jρ')/2 and η > 0 with ρ' + 2η < ρ. For large k, |w_k − w| < η, B_{ρ'}(w_k) ⊆ closedBall w (ρ' + η) ⊆ U_{S_k} by (ix), and every y ∈ spt S_k ∩ B_{ρ'}(w_k) has |q_Π(y − w_k)| < τ: otherwise, for infinitely many k there would be such y_k with |q_Π(y_k − w_k)| ≥ τ, a limit point y would lie in spt S (by (T3s)) ∩ closedBall w ρ' ⊆ B_ρ(w) with |q_Π(y − w)| ≥ τ > s, contradicting the definition of s. Then (ρ', Π) witnesses w_k ∈ R_j(φ_{S_k}) (sup ≤ τ < β_jρ'), a contradiction.
7. (A3: applying Appendix A.4.) By the sibling abstract_dimension_reduction (with Q := 1, F, sing := sing_j), (I) or (II) holds. Suppose (II) with d = n − 1: there are ψ = φ_S ∈ F and L with dim L = n − 1, sing_j ψ = L and ψ(y + λx) = ψ(x) for y ∈ L, λ > 0. Since sing_j 0 = ∅ ≠ L, ψ ≠ 0; ψ is homogeneous, so S has parameter 0 by (f), S is minimizing in ℝ^P with ∂S = 0, and Θ_S = ϑ_S is invariant under w ↦ y + λw. By the sibling child cone_splitting (dim L = n − 1 < n) there is S₀ ∈ 𝒟_1(ℝ^P), minimizing, ∂S₀ = 0, a cone, with spt S₀ ⊆ L^⊥ and t + y ∈ spt S ⟺ y ∈ spt S₀; by the sibling child one_dim_cones, spt S₀ ⊆ span{e} for some e. Hence spt S ⊆ L + span{e}, a subspace of dimension ≤ n, contained in some n-dimensional subspace Π''. Then U(ψ) = ℝ^P and every w ∈ spt ψ = spt S is witnessed in R_j(ψ) by (1, Π''), so sing_j ψ = ∅ ≠ L: a contradiction. Hence (I) holds or d ≤ n − 2, and since sing_j φ_{T'} ∩ B_1(0) = (spt T' ∩ B_1(0)) ∖ R_j(φ_{T'}) (B_1(0) ⊆ U(φ_{T'}) = B_2(0)), μH[n − 2 + α]((spt T' ∩ B_1(0)) ∖ R_j(φ_{T'})) = 0 for all α > 0 (n − 2 + α = d + (n − 2 − d + α)); for n = 1 case (II) is impossible, so this set is empty. Put G_{z,r} := spt T' ∩ B_1(0) ∩ ∩_j R_j(φ_{T'}) and F'_{z,r} := (spt T' ∩ B_1(0)) ∖ G_{z,r} = ∪_j((spt T' ∩ B_1(0)) ∖ R_j(φ_{T'})), and F_{z,r} := z + rF'_{z,r}. Then μH[n − 2 + α](F_{z,r}) = r^{n−2+α}μH[n − 2 + α](F'_{z,r}) = 0 for n ≥ 2 and α > 0, and F_{z,r} = ∅ for n = 1.
8. (A4: tangent planes at flat points; corrected (13).) Let w ∈ G_{z,r} and x := z + rw ∈ spt T. For each j there are ρ_j ∈ (0, 2] and Π_j with B_{ρ_j}(w) ⊆ B_2(0) and |q_{Π_j}(y − w)| < 2^{−j}ρ_j for y ∈ spt T' ∩ B_{ρ_j}(w). Pass to a subsequence with Π_j → Π (compactness of the Grassmannian; ‖q_{Π_j} − q_Π‖ → 0) and ρ_j → ρ_∞ ∈ [0, 2]. Case ρ_∞ > 0: every y ∈ spt T' ∩ B_{ρ_∞/2}(w) lies in B_{ρ_j}(w) for large j, so |q_Π(y − w)| = lim|q_{Π_j}(y − w)| = 0, i.e. spt T' ∩ B_{ρ_∞/2}(w) ⊆ w + Π. By the constancy theorem (Simon Ch. 6, 2.34, with ∂T' = 0 and the connectedness of (w + Π) ∩ B_{ρ_∞/2}(w)), T' = c₀[[w + Π]] in B_{ρ_∞/2}(w) for some c₀ ∈ ℤ (T' is integer multiplicity; [[Π]] carries a fixed orientation), and c₀ ≠ 0 as w ∈ spt T'. Then, with λ_i := r/i, blowUp T x λ_i = η_{w,1/i#}T' equals c₀[[Π]] on B_{iρ_∞/2}(0), so blowUp T x λ_i ⇀ C := c₀[[Π]] (ConvergesWeakly), spt C = Π and dim Π = n: HasTangentPlaneAt T x. Case ρ_∞ = 0: by the sibling density_and_tangent_cones (2) at x ∈ spt T (boundarySupport T = ∅) with the scales rρ_j → 0, a further subsequence and a minimizing cone C satisfy blowUp T x (rρ_j) ⇀ C with mass measure convergence and HasMassDensity C 0 Θ(x), Θ(x) ≥ 1; so 0 ∈ spt C and C ≠ 0; ∂C = 0 as a weak limit of cycles. Since B_{ρ_j}(w) ⊆ B_2(0), blowUp T x (rρ_j) = η_{w,ρ_j#}T' on η_{w,ρ_j}(B_2(0)) ⊇ B_1(0), and its support in B_1(0) lies in {v : |q_{Π_j}(v)| < 2^{−j}} ⊆ {v : |q_Π(v)| < 2^{−j} + ‖q_{Π_j} − q_Π‖}. If v ∈ spt C ∩ B_1(0), lower semicontinuity of mass on open sets gives points of spt(blowUp T x (rρ_j)) converging to v, so |q_Π(v)| = 0: spt C ∩ B_1(0) ⊆ Π, and since spt C is a cone, spt C ⊆ Π. By constancy (∂C = 0, C integer multiplicity, Π connected), C = c₀[[Π]] with c₀ ∈ ℤ ∖ {0}, so spt C = Π: HasTangentPlaneAt T x (IsTangentConeAt with the scales rρ_j).
9. (A5: assembly.) Put F := E ∪ ∪_{(z,r)∈𝒞}F_{z,r}, so E ⊆ F. For α > 0: μH[n − 2 + α](E) = 0 (for n ≥ 3 by step 4 with n − 2 + α = n − 3 + (1 + α); for n ≤ 2, E = ∅), and μH[n − 2 + α](F_{z,r}) = 0 (step 7); by countable subadditivity μH[n − 2 + α](F) = 0 (for n = 1, F = ∅). Let x ∈ spt T ∖ F and pick (z, r) ∈ 𝒞 with x ∈ B_r(z). Then μ_T(B_{2r}(z)) > 0, so T' ≠ 0, and w := (x − z)/r ∈ spt T' ∩ B_1(0) with w ∉ F'_{z,r} (as x ∉ F_{z,r}); hence w ∈ G_{z,r}, and step 8 gives HasTangentPlaneAt T x. Together with step 1 (integer densities on U ∖ E) and step 4, this proves IntegerDensityAndTangentPlanes.
proof_key_steps: n = 0: T = 0 by zero_dim_vanishing, take E = F = ∅; for n ≥ 1, monotonicity gives an upper semicontinuous density Θ with Θ ≥ 1 on spt T, and E := {Θ ∉ ℤ}.

7.3.3(1): cover E by the sets E_{m,β}; uniform density bounds pass to zero-scale limits; threshold_reduction with c = m − 1 + β, d₀ = n − 2, where (H1) fails by integrality and (H2) fails by cone_splitting with one_dim_cones (n − d = 1) or White's classification (n − d = 2).

7.3.3(2): per rational ball, Simon's class 𝒯 with domains recovered from mass and barycenter; density functions with the correct normalization ∫_K ϑ_S dμH[n] = c_n⁻¹·μ_S(K), tangent cones of members obtained by an explicit diagonal selection and a countable-test criterion for limits on ℝ^P with exhausting domains; the flatness maps sing_j satisfy A.1–A.3, and an (n−1)-dimensional extremal is a plane by cone_splitting and one_dim_cones, so the non-flat sets are H^{n−2+α}-null.
Points flat at all scales β_j = 2^{−j} have a tangent plane, by constancy (ρ_∞ > 0) or by flatness of a tangent cone (ρ_∞ = 0).
F := E ∪ ∪F_{z,r} is H^{n−2+α}-null, contains E, and every x ∈ spt T ∖ F has a tangent plane.

subproblems.title: Simon 7.4.4: near a point of density below 2 the singular set is H^{n−2+α}-null
subproblems.statement: SingularSetSmallWhereDensityBelowTwo of the frozen contract (Simon 7.4.4). For all n, k, ℓ ∈ ℕ with ℓ ≤ k, all sets U, N ⊆ ℝ^{n+k} and every T ∈ 𝒟_n(U): if U is open, N is an embedded C² (n+ℓ)-dimensional submanifold, (closure N ∖ N) ∩ U = ∅, T is minimizing in U ∩ N, spt T ⊆ U ∩ N and ∂T = 0 in U, then for every ξ ∈ spt T and every real θ with HasMassDensity T ξ θ and θ < 2 there is ρ > 0 such that μH[n − 2 + α](sing T ∩ B_ρ(ξ)) = 0 for every real α > 0 (sing T = singularSet T = spt T ∖ regularSet T).
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent steps 0 and B1–B3 (Simon 7.4.4 and its proof, chapter-07.txt lines 635–684), with departure [D3]: the book's 4.4(8) (sing S = {Θ ≥ 1 + δ}, from Allard's theorem) is proved from the gap lemma (sibling child density_gap) and the sibling density_one_implies_regular. P := n + k; μ_A is the measure of any representation of an integer multiplicity A (sibling child im_mass_measure: all representations have the same measure (c), M_W(A) = μ_A(W) for open W (a), spt A = spt μ_A (b)); Θ_A := Θ^n(μ_A, ·); ω_n := unitBallVolume n.
0. (n = 0.) By the sibling child zero_dim_vanishing (A := U ∩ N), T = 0, so spt T = ∅ and the statement is vacuous. From now on n ≥ 1, so boundarySupport T = ∅.
1. (B1: choice of the ball; book (1).) Let ξ ∈ spt T and HasMassDensity T ξ θ with θ < 2. By the sibling child monotonicity (d := n + ℓ) there is an upper semicontinuous Θ on U with HasMassDensity T x (Θ(x)) for x ∈ U, Θ ≥ 1 on spt T, and the monotonicity of e^{Λ_Kρ}ρ^{−n}μ_T(B_ρ(y)) on balls closedBall y R ⊆ K for each compact K ⊆ U; densities are unique, so Θ(ξ) = θ. Put θ' := (2 + θ)/2 < 2 and θ₁ := (θ + θ')/2 ∈ (θ, θ'). By upper semicontinuity choose σ > 0 with closedBall ξ (4σ) ⊆ U and Θ < θ₁ on closedBall ξ (4σ). By the uniform density bound (parent T10; K := closedBall ξ (3σ/2), K'' := closedBall ξ (4σ)): for y ∈ K choose ρ_y ∈ (0, σ) with e^{Λρ_y}μ_T(B_{ρ_y}(y))/(ω_nρ_y^n) < θ₁ (Λ := Λ_{K''}) and τ_y ∈ (0, ρ_y) with θ₁(ρ_y/(ρ_y − τ_y))^n ≤ θ'; for |y' − y| < τ_y and ρ < ρ_y − τ_y, monotonicity at y' and B_{ρ_y−τ_y}(y') ⊆ B_{ρ_y}(y) give μ_T(B_ρ(y')) ≤ θ'ω_nρ^n; covering K by finitely many B_{τ_y}(y) yields ρ₀ > 0 with μ_T(B_ρ(y)) ≤ θ'ω_nρ^n for y ∈ closedBall ξ (3σ/2) and ρ < ρ₀. In particular Θ ≤ θ' < 2 on B_{3σ/2}(ξ).
2. (Densities of admissible zero-scale limits.) Let x_i ∈ B_σ(ξ), λ_i → 0⁺, and S ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with blowUp T x_i λ_i ⇀ S (ConvergesWeakly), S minimizing in ℝ^P with ∂S = 0. For w ∈ ℝ^P and ρ > 0 and large i, x_i + λ_iw ∈ B_{3σ/2}(ξ), λ_iρ < ρ₀ and M_{B_ρ(w)}(blowUp T x_i λ_i) = λ_i^{−n}M_{B_{λ_iρ}(x_i+λ_iw)}(T) ≤ θ'ω_nρ^n; since S(ω) = lim currentEval(blowUp T x_i λ_i, ω) for each admissible ω, M_{B_ρ(w)}(S) ≤ θ'ω_nρ^n. Θ_S exists everywhere (sibling child monotonicity with U = N = ℝ^P), so Θ_S ≤ θ' < 2 everywhere; and Θ_S equals the multiplicity of S μ_S-a.e. (Simon Ch. 3, Theorem 1.9; Ch. 4, Remark 1.8(2)), a positive integer.
3. (B2: sing T near ξ is a density superlevel set; book (8), [D3].) Let δ > 0 be given by the sibling child density_gap for (P, j) := (n + k, n). Claim: for x ∈ spt T ∩ B_σ(ξ), x ∈ reg T ⟺ Θ(x) < 1 + δ. (⇐) If Θ(x) < 1 + δ: by the sibling density_and_tangent_cones (2) at x ∈ spt T ∖ boundarySupport T (with any λ_j → 0⁺) there is a cone C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P), minimizing in ℝ^P, with blowUp T x λ_j ⇀ C along a subsequence and HasMassDensity C 0 Θ(x); ∂C = 0 because C(dω) = lim(blowUp T x λ_j)(dω) = 0. By density_gap, Θ(x) ≤ 1; with Θ ≥ 1 on spt T, Θ(x) = 1. Apply the sibling density_one_implies_regular (DAG node root.density_one_implies_regular-a1) with Ts :≡ T (constant sequence), ys :≡ x, y := x: the hypotheses hold (T minimizing in U ∩ N, supports in N, BoundaryVanishes, sup_j M_W(T) = μ_T(W) < ∞ for W ⊂⊂ U, constant sequences converge weakly, x ∈ N ∩ U, HasMassDensity T x 1, x ∈ spt T), so x ∈ reg T. (⇒) If x ∈ reg T, the sibling child regular_point_density gives m ∈ ℕ, m ≥ 1, with HasMassDensity T x m, so Θ(x) = m; since Θ(x) ≤ θ' < 2 (step 1), m = 1 < 1 + δ. Moreover every x ∈ B_σ(ξ) with Θ(x) ≥ 1 + δ > 0 lies in spt T (off spt T the density is 0). Hence sing T ∩ B_σ(ξ) = {x ∈ B_σ(ξ) : Θ(x) ≥ 1 + δ} = {x ∈ B_σ(ξ) : ∃ θ'' ≥ 1 + δ, HasMassDensity T x θ''}.
4. (B3: dimension reduction; book lines 641–684.) Apply the sibling child threshold_reduction with z := ξ, r := σ (closedBall ξ (2σ) ⊆ U), c := 1 + δ > 0 and d₀ := n − 1. Hypothesis (H1): let S be an admissible zero-scale limit (centres in B_σ(ξ), minimizing, ∂S = 0) with Θ_S = c'·1_Q for an n-dimensional subspace Q and c' ≥ 1 + δ. As c' > 0, Q ⊆ spt S, so μ_S ≠ 0 and by step 2 some y has Θ_S(y) ∈ ℤ_{≥1}; then y ∈ Q and c' = Θ_S(y) is an integer with 1 + δ ≤ c' ≤ θ' < 2: impossible. Hypothesis (H2): let S be an admissible zero-scale limit and L a subspace with n − 1 ≤ dim L < n (so dim L = n − 1), L-invariant density function and {Θ_S ≥ 1 + δ} = L. As 0 ∈ L, Θ_S(0) ≥ 1 + δ, and Θ_S(0) ≤ θ' < 2 by step 2. By the sibling child cone_splitting there is S₀ ∈ 𝒟_1(ℝ^P) (n − dim L = 1), minimizing in ℝ^P, ∂S₀ = 0, a cone, with Θ_S(0) = Θ_{S₀}(0); by the sibling child one_dim_cones (S₀ transported to degree 1) there are e, m' ∈ ℕ with HasMassDensity S₀ 0 m' (0 ∈ span{e}), so Θ_S(0) = m' ∈ ℕ ∩ [1 + δ, θ'] = ∅: impossible. (For n = 1 this is the case dim L = 0, and the argument is the same.) Hence threshold_reduction gives: if n ≥ 2 (d₀ = n − 1 ≥ 1), μH[(n − 1) − 1 + α](Z) = μH[n − 2 + α](Z) = 0 for every α > 0, and if n = 1 (d₀ = 0), Z = ∅, where Z := {x ∈ B_σ(ξ) : ∃ θ'' ≥ 1 + δ, HasMassDensity T x θ''} = sing T ∩ B_σ(ξ) (step 3).
5. (Conclusion.) Take ρ := σ > 0. For every α > 0, μH[n − 2 + α](singularSet T ∩ B_ρ(ξ)) = 0 (for n = 1 the set is empty, which covers the negative exponents).
proof_key_steps: n = 0: T = 0 and the statement is vacuous; for n ≥ 1 pick σ with Θ ≤ θ' < 2 near ξ and the uniform bound μ_T(B_ρ(y)) ≤ θ'ω_nρ^n, which passes to zero-scale limits.
Gap lemma + density_one_implies_regular + regular_point_density: in B_σ(ξ), x ∈ reg T ⇔ Θ(x) < 1 + δ, so sing T ∩ B_σ(ξ) = {Θ ≥ 1 + δ}.

threshold_reduction with c = 1 + δ and d₀ = n − 1: (H1) fails since integer densities below 2 are ≤ 1, (H2) fails since an (n−1)-invariant cone splits off a 1-dimensional cone, which by one_dim_cones has integer vertex density.
Hence μH[n−2+α](sing T ∩ B_σ(ξ)) = 0 (empty set for n = 1); take ρ := σ.

subproblems.title: Simon 7.5.8: regularity of codimension-one minimizing boundaries
subproblems.statement: CodimensionOneRegularity of the frozen contract (Simon 7.5.8, with README erratum 7). For all n, k ∈ ℕ, all sets U, N, E ⊆ ℝ^{n+k}, every map ξ_N : ℝ^{n+k} → Λ_{n+1}(ℝ^{n+k}) (MultiVector (n+k) (n+1)) and every T ∈ 𝒟_n(U): if U is open, InClassO n U N ξ_N (N an embedded C² (n+1)-dimensional submanifold, ξ_N a continuous orientation of N, (closure N ∖ N) ∩ U = ∅, N ∩ U ≠ ∅), E is a measurable set with E ⊆ N ∩ U, T(ω) = ∫_E ξ_N(x)(dω(x)) dH^{n+1}(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) (IsBoundaryOfRegion T E ξ_N), and T is minimizing in N ∩ U, then: (a) singularSet T = ∅ if n ≤ 6; (b) singularSet T ∩ K is finite for every compact K ⊆ U if n = 7; (c) μH[n − 7 + α](singularSet T) = 0 for every real α > 0 if n > 7.
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent steps 0 and C0–C6 (Simon 7.5.8 and its proof, chapter-07.txt lines 919–974 with footnote 5; 5.2(‡) and 5.3–5.4(3), lines 757–860; Appendix B, B.1, B.2 and its printed proof, chapter-07-source.txt lines 1256–1539), with departures [D3] (gap lemma and density_one_implies_regular instead of Allard along sequences), [D4] (zero-scale limits with moving centres lie in affine planes T_xN − a; the offset plane is treated with the cutoff radius R + |a| + 2, and the projected-current identity and the uniform perimeter bound are proved before BV compactness), [D5] (δ below every gap constant used; the factor S₀ is handled through densities; the hypotheses of B.2 are verified). P := n + k; μ_A is the measure of any representation of an integer multiplicity A (sibling child im_mass_measure: all representations have the same measure (c), M_W(A) = μ_A(W) for open W (a), spt A = spt μ_A (b)); Θ_A := Θ^n(μ_A, ·); H^m := μHE[m]; ω_n := unitBallVolume n; η_{y,λ}(w) := λ^{−1}(w − y).
0. (C0: setting; n = 0.) T is integer multiplicity (first conjunct of IsMinimizingIn). If ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) vanishes near closure(E), then dω = 0 on E and T(ω) = 0; hence spt T ⊆ closure(E) ∩ U ⊆ closure(N) ∩ U ⊆ N (as (closure N ∖ N) ∩ U = ∅). If n = 0, the sibling child zero_dim_vanishing (A := N ∩ U, spt T ⊆ N ∩ U) gives T = 0, so singularSet T = ∅ ⊆ spt T = ∅; (a) holds and (b), (c) are vacuous. Assume n ≥ 1. Then k ≥ 1 (N ∩ U ≠ ∅ and an embedded (n+1)-dimensional submanifold of ℝ^{n+k} requires n + 1 ≤ n + k); N is an embedded C² (n + ℓ)-submanifold with ℓ := 1 ≤ k; spt T ⊆ U ∩ N; T is minimizing in U ∩ N = N ∩ U; ∂T = 0 since T(dω) = ∫_E ξ_N(d(dω)) dH^{n+1} = 0. So T satisfies the hypotheses of the sibling children monotonicity (d := n + 1) and threshold_reduction (ℓ := 1), and of the siblings density_and_tangent_cones and density_one_implies_regular. Let Θ be the upper semicontinuous density of T on U given by monotonicity (iii); Θ ≥ 1 on spt T.
1. (C1: multiplicity one; Simon 5.2(‡).) Θ = 1 μ_T-a.e. Proof: let y ∈ N ∩ U and Φ a C² diffeomorphism from an open W ∋ y (W ⊆ U) onto an open subset of ℝ^P with Φ(W ∩ N) = G × {0}, G ⊆ ℝ^{n+1} open, orientation preserving from ξ_N to the standard orientation. Then Φ_#(T⌞W) = ∂[[Φ(E ∩ W)]] in Φ(W) (change of variables in the defining integral), and since T has locally finite mass, Φ(E ∩ W) has locally finite perimeter in G (Simon Ch. 6, 2.35). By De Giorgi's structure theorem (Ch. 3, 4.3), ∂[[Φ(E ∩ W)]] is the integer multiplicity current carried by the reduced boundary with multiplicity 1; pushing back by Φ^{−1} (multiplicity is preserved by C¹ diffeomorphisms, Ch. 6, 3.3–3.9), T has multiplicity 1 H^n-a.e. on its carrier in W, and Θ = multiplicity = 1 μ_T-a.e. (Ch. 3, Theorem 1.9; Ch. 4, Remark 1.8(2)). Cover N ∩ U by countably many such W.
2. (C4: sing T is the superlevel set {Θ ≥ 1 + δ}.) For 1 ≤ j ≤ n let δ_j > 0 be given by the sibling child density_gap for (P, j), and put δ := min_{1≤j≤n} δ_j > 0. For x ∈ spt T: x ∈ reg T ⟺ Θ(x) < 1 + δ. (⇐) If Θ(x) < 1 + δ, a tangent cone C of T at x (sibling density_and_tangent_cones (2); C minimizing in ℝ^P, a cone, ∂C = 0 as a weak limit of cycles, HasMassDensity C 0 Θ(x)) has vertex density < 1 + δ_n, so density_gap gives Θ(x) ≤ 1, hence Θ(x) = 1, and the sibling density_one_implies_regular with constant sequences (Ts :≡ T, ys :≡ x, y := x) gives x ∈ reg T. (⇒) If x ∈ reg T, the sibling child regular_point_density gives m ≥ 1 and ρ > 0 with Θ = m on spt T ∩ B_ρ(x); since μ_T(B_ρ(x)) > 0 (x ∈ spt T), μ_T(B_ρ(x) ∖ spt T) = 0 and Θ = 1 μ_T-a.e. (step 1), m = 1, so Θ(x) = 1 < 1 + δ. As points with Θ ≥ 1 + δ > 0 lie in spt T, sing T = {x ∈ U : Θ(x) ≥ 1 + δ}.
3. (C2(ii): zero-scale limits lie in offset planes and have multiplicity one; [D4].) Claim: let x_i ∈ U converge to x ∈ U, λ_i > 0, λ_i → 0, S_i := blowUp T x_i λ_i, and S ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with S_i ⇀ S (ConvergesWeakly), S ≠ 0. Then x ∈ N, and there are a ∈ (T_xN)^⊥ and an H^{n+1}-measurable F ⊆ A := T_xN − a of locally finite perimeter in A with S = ∂[[F]] in ℝ^P, where [[F]](β) := ∫_F ξ_A(β) dH^{n+1} and ξ_A := ξ_N(x) orients A; in particular spt S ⊆ A and Θ_S = 1 μ_S-a.e. Proof. (α) Put N_i := η_{x_i,λ_i}(N), E_i := η_{x_i,λ_i}(E), ξ_i(w) := ξ_N(x_i + λ_iw). By the change of variables w = x_i + λ_iv in the defining integral (η_{x_i,λ_i}^#(dω) = λ_i^{−(n+1)}dω∘η_{x_i,λ_i}, dH^{n+1}(w) = λ_i^{n+1}dH^{n+1}(v)), S_i(ω) = ∫_{E_i} ξ_i(dω) dH^{n+1} for ω ∈ 𝒟^n(η_{x_i,λ_i}(U)), and spt S_i ⊆ N_i. Choose δ₀ > 0 with closedBall x (2δ₀) ⊆ U and Λ for K := closedBall x (2δ₀) (monotonicity (i)); for |x_i − x| < δ₀ and λ_iρ ≤ δ₀/2, μ_{S_i}(B_ρ(0)) = λ_i^{−n}μ_T(B_{λ_iρ}(x_i)) ≤ c_*ρ^n with c_* := e^{Λδ₀}(2/δ₀)^nμ_T(K). If dist(x_i, N)/λ_i were unbounded, then along a subsequence every ball B_R(0) would eventually miss N_i ⊇ spt S_i and S = 0. Hence dist(x_i, N) ≤ C₀λ_i for some C₀ ≥ 1 and all i, and x ∈ closure(N) ∩ U ⊆ N. (β) Let Π₀ := T_xN, p the orthogonal projection onto Π₀ and p^⊥ := I − p. As N is an embedded C² submanifold, relatively closed in U, there are δ₁, δ₂ > 0 and u ∈ C²(Π₀ ∩ B_{δ₁}(0); Π₀^⊥) with u(0) = 0, Du(0) = 0, |Du| ≤ 1, |u| < δ₂, such that the open cylinder Z := {x + v + h : v ∈ Π₀, |v| < δ₁, h ∈ Π₀^⊥, |h| < δ₂} lies in U and N ∩ Z = {x + v + u(v) : v ∈ Π₀, |v| < δ₁}; moreover ξ_N(x + v + u(v)) = Λ_{n+1}(I + Du(v))ξ_A/|Λ_{n+1}(I + Du(v))ξ_A| (two continuous unit orientations of the tangent planes of a connected graph that agree at v = 0). Write x_i − x = s_i + t_i (s_i ∈ Π₀, t_i ∈ Π₀^⊥) and, for w ∈ Π₀ with |s_i + λ_iw| < δ₁, G_i(w) := w + g_i(w), g_i(w) := λ_i^{−1}(u(s_i + λ_iw) − t_i). Then η_{x_i,λ_i}(x + v + u(v)) = G_i(λ_i^{−1}(v − s_i)), so η_{x_i,λ_i}(N ∩ Z) = G_i(dom G_i); p∘G_i = id, p^⊥∘G_i = g_i, DG_i(w) = I + Du(s_i + λ_iw) on Π₀, and ξ_i(G_i(w)) = Λ_{n+1}DG_i(w)ξ_A/J_i(w) with J_i(w) := |Λ_{n+1}DG_i(w)ξ_A| the Jacobian of G_i. (γ) Choose p_i ∈ N with |p_i − x_i| ≤ 2C₀λ_i; for large i, p_i = x + v_i + u(v_i) ∈ Z and w_i := λ_i^{−1}(v_i − s_i) satisfies G_i(w_i) = η_{x_i,λ_i}(p_i), so |w_i| ≤ 2C₀ and |g_i(w_i)| ≤ 2C₀; since |Dg_i| ≤ 1, |g_i(0)| ≤ 4C₀. Pass to a subsequence with g_i(0) → −a; then a ∈ Π₀^⊥, and because Dg_i(w) = Du(s_i + λ_iw) → 0 uniformly on bounded sets, G_i → G, G(w) := w − a, in C¹ on Π₀ ∩ closedBall 0 R' for every R'. Put A := G(Π₀) = Π₀ − a, oriented by ξ_A. (δ) Fix R ≥ 1, R₁ := R + |a| + 2 and C_R := {y : |p(y)| < R, |p^⊥(y)| < |a| + 1} ⊆ B_{R₁}(0). For all large i: B_{λ_iR₁}(x_i) ⊆ Z, B_{R₁}(0) ⊆ η_{x_i,λ_i}(U), λ_iR₁ ≤ δ₀/2, Π₀ ∩ closedBall 0 R₁ ⊆ dom G_i, and |g_i(w) + a| < 1/4 for |w| ≤ R₁. For these i: (δ1) N_i ∩ B_{R₁}(0) = η_{x_i,λ_i}(N ∩ B_{λ_iR₁}(x_i)) ⊆ G_i(dom G_i); (δ2) N_i ∩ C_R = G_i(Π₀ ∩ B_R(0)) (a point y of the left side lies in B_{R₁}(0), so y = G_i(w) with |w| = |p(y)| < R; conversely, for |w| < R, |p^⊥(G_i(w))| = |g_i(w)| < |a| + 1/4); (δ3) N_i ∩ B_R(0) ⊆ G_i(Π₀ ∩ B_R(0)) ⊆ {y : |p^⊥(y)| < |a| + 1/4}. (ε) Let F_i' := {w ∈ dom G_i : G_i(w) ∈ E_i} and F_i := G(F_i') ⊆ A. For ω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P) with tsupport ω ⊆ C_R and large i, (α), (δ2), the area formula for the injective C¹ map G_i on Π₀ ∩ B_R(0) and (β) give S_i(ω) = ∫_{E_i∩C_R} ξ_i(dω) dH^{n+1} = ∫_{F_i'∩B_R(0)} ξ_i(G_i(w))(dω(G_i(w)))J_i(w) dH^{n+1}(w) = ∫_{F_i'∩B_R(0)} ξ_A((G_i^#dω)(w)) dH^{n+1}(w). Let π_A := G∘p = p − a and ζ(y) := χ(|p^⊥(y)|) with χ ∈ C^∞(ℝ; [0, 1]), χ = 1 on (−∞, |a| + 3/4], χ = 0 on [|a| + 7/8, ∞) (ζ is smooth because χ is constant near 0). For every n-form α̃ ∈ 𝒟^n(A ∩ B_R(−a)) (A ∩ B_R(−a) = G(Π₀ ∩ B_R(0)) = A ∩ C_R), ω := ζ·π_A^#α̃ belongs to 𝒟^n(ℝ^P) with tsupport ω ⊆ C_R, and G_i^#ω = χ(|g_i|)(π_A∘G_i)^#α̃ = G^#α̃ on Π₀ ∩ B_R(0) (π_A∘G_i = G and |g_i| < |a| + 1/4 there); hence S_i(ζ·π_A^#α̃) = ∫_{F_i'∩B_R(0)} ξ_A(G^#dα̃) dH^{n+1} = ∫_{F_i} ξ_A(dα̃) dH^{n+1} = ∂[[F_i]](α̃) (G is a translation): ∂[[F_i]] = π_{A#}(ζS_i) on A ∩ B_R(−a). (ζ) If moreover |α̃| ≤ 1 pointwise, then |ζπ_A^#α̃| ≤ 1 (π_A is an orthogonal projection followed by a translation, 0 ≤ ζ ≤ 1), so |∂[[F_i]](α̃)| ≤ M_{C_R}(S_i) ≤ μ_{S_i}(B_{R₁}(0)) ≤ c_*R₁^n. Identifying A with ℝ^{n+1} (oriented by ξ_A), n-forms α̃ with |α̃| ≤ 1 correspond to vector fields φ with |φ| ≤ 1 and ξ_A(dα̃) = div φ, so the perimeter of F_i in A ∩ B_R(−a) (Ch. 2, 2.1; smooth fields suffice by mollification) is at most c_*(R + |a| + 2)^n for all large i ≥ i_R, and H^{n+1}(F_i ∩ B_R(−a)) ≤ ω_{n+1}R^{n+1}. (η) For R = 1, 2, … apply the BV compactness theorem (Ch. 2, 2.6) on A ∩ B_{R+1}(−a) to the tail i ≥ i_{R+1} of the current subsequence; a diagonal subsequence gives an H^{n+1}-measurable F ⊆ A with 1_{F_i} → 1_F in L¹(A ∩ B_R(−a)) for every R, and F has locally finite perimeter in A by lower semicontinuity of the variation (Ch. 2, §2; SimonGMT Chapter02.bvVariationOn_le_liminf_of_locallyL1). (θ) Let ω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P) with tsupport ω ⊆ B_R(0) (R ∈ ℕ) and write ω = ζω + (1 − ζ)ω. (1 − ζ)ω vanishes on the open set {|p^⊥| < |a| + 3/4}, which contains N_i ∩ B_R(0) for large i (δ3) and contains A (|p^⊥| = |a| on A); hence S_i((1 − ζ)ω) = 0 and ∂[[F]]((1 − ζ)ω) = [[F]](d((1 − ζ)ω)) = 0. Since tsupport(ζω) ⊆ C_R, (ε) gives S_i(ζω) = ∫_{F_i'∩B_R(0)} ξ_A(G_i^#d(ζω)) dH^{n+1}; as 1_{F_i'} = 1_{F_i}∘G → 1_F∘G in L¹(Π₀ ∩ B_R(0)) and G_i^#d(ζω) → G^#d(ζω) uniformly on Π₀ ∩ closedBall 0 R, S_i(ζω) → ∫_{G^{−1}(F)∩B_R(0)} ξ_A(G^#d(ζω)) dH^{n+1} = [[F]](d(ζω)) = ∂[[F]](ζω). As S_i ⇀ S, S(ω) = ∂[[F]](ω). Thus S = ∂[[F]], spt S ⊆ closure(F) ⊆ A, and De Giorgi's structure theorem in the plane A (Ch. 3, 4.3; as in step 1 with N replaced by A) gives μ_S = H^n⌞∂*F, so Θ_S = 1 μ_S-a.e.
4. (C2(iii): cones lie in linear planes.) If in step 3 S is moreover a cone, then spt S is a nonempty closed cone, so 0 ∈ spt S ⊆ A = Π₀ − a, i.e. a ∈ Π₀ ∩ Π₀^⊥ = {0}: spt S ⊆ T_xN, a linear (n+1)-dimensional subspace.
5. (C5: hypotheses of threshold_reduction.) Fix z, r with closedBall z (2r) ⊆ U and apply the sibling child threshold_reduction (ℓ := 1) with c := 1 + δ and d₀ := n − 6 (natural subtraction). Let S be an admissible zero-scale limit: S = lim blowUp T x_i λ_i (ConvergesWeakly) with x_i ∈ B_r(z), λ_i → 0⁺, S minimizing in ℝ^P with ∂S = 0. Passing to a subsequence, x_i → x ∈ closedBall z r ⊆ U, so steps 3 and 4 apply to S whenever S ≠ 0. Hypothesis (H1): if Θ_S = c'·1_Q with Q an n-dimensional subspace and c' ≥ 1 + δ, then Q ⊆ spt S (c' > 0), so S ≠ 0, and by step 3 Θ_S = 1 μ_S-a.e.; since μ_S ≠ 0 there is y with Θ_S(y) = 1 ∈ {0, c'}, so c' = 1 < 1 + δ: impossible. Hypothesis (H2): suppose L is a subspace with d₀ ≤ d := dim L < n, Θ_S invariant under w ↦ y + λw (y ∈ L, λ > 0), and {Θ_S ≥ 1 + δ} = L. As 0 ∈ L, Θ_S(0) ≥ 1 + δ > 0, so S ≠ 0. By the sibling child cone_splitting, S is a cone and there is S₀ ∈ 𝒟_{n'}(ℝ^P), n' := n − d, minimizing in ℝ^P, ∂S₀ = 0, a cone, spt S₀ ⊆ L^⊥, with t + y ∈ spt S ⟺ y ∈ spt S₀ and Θ_S(t + y) = Θ_{S₀}(y) for t ∈ L, y ∈ L^⊥. By step 4, spt S ⊆ A₀' := T_xN, a linear (n+1)-dimensional subspace; L ⊆ spt S (Θ_S ≥ 1 + δ > 0 on L), so L ⊆ A₀', and spt S₀ ⊆ A₀ := A₀' ∩ L^⊥ (y ∈ spt S₀ ⟹ y = 0 + y ∈ spt S), a linear subspace of dimension n' + 1. Moreover Θ_{S₀}(0) = Θ_S(0) ≥ 1 + δ, and for y ∈ L^⊥ ∖ {0} we have y ∉ L, so Θ_{S₀}(y) = Θ_S(y) < 1 + δ. Since d₀ ≤ d ≤ n − 1, 1 ≤ n' ≤ 6. Case n' = 1: the sibling child one_dim_cones (S₀ transported to degree 1) gives e, m' with spt S₀ ⊆ span{e} and HasMassDensity S₀ y m' for y ∈ span{e}; then m' = Θ_{S₀}(0) ≥ 1 + δ > 0, so |e| = 1, e ∈ spt S₀ ⊆ L^⊥ (positive density), e ≠ 0, and m' = Θ_{S₀}(e) < 1 + δ: impossible. Case 2 ≤ n' ≤ 6: (α) every y ∈ spt S₀ ∖ {0} is a regular point: by the sibling density_and_tangent_cones (2) applied to S₀ (dimension n', U = N = ℝ^P, after transporting along Euclid P = Euclid (n' + (P − n'))), S₀ has at y a minimizing tangent cone C_y with ∂C_y = 0 and HasMassDensity C_y 0 Θ_{S₀}(y); as Θ_{S₀}(y) < 1 + δ ≤ 1 + δ_{n'}, density_gap gives Θ_{S₀}(y) ≤ 1, so Θ_{S₀}(y) = 1 (monotonicity (iv)), and the sibling density_one_implies_regular with constant sequences (dimension n', U = N = ℝ^P) gives y ∈ reg S₀ (and the sibling child regular_point_density then gives Θ_{S₀} ≡ 1 on spt S₀ near y). (β) Let M := spt S₀ ∖ {0} ⊆ A₀, and identify A₀ with ℝ^{n'+1} by a linear isometry. M ≠ ∅ (otherwise μ_{S₀} would be carried by {0}, so S₀ = 0 as n' ≥ 1, contradicting Θ_{S₀}(0) > 0), M is a cone, and closure(M) ∖ M = {0}. The hypotheses of Simon's Theorem B.2 hold for M in A₀ ≅ ℝ^{n'+1}: (i) M is an embedded C¹ hypersurface of A₀: by (α), for each y ∈ M there are ρ_y > 0, m_y ∈ ℤ ∖ {0} and an embedded C¹ n'-submanifold M_y ∋ y with S₀ = m_y[[M_y]] in B_{ρ_y}(y); by properness and injectivity of the chart of M_y at y (as in step 2 of the proof of regular_point_density), M_y is relatively closed in a small ball B_{ρ'}(y), 0 < ρ' ≤ min(ρ_y, |y|)/2 (so 0 ∉ B_{ρ'}(y)); re-proved here exactly as in steps 3–4 of that proof (the mass identity M_{B_s(w)}(S₀) = |m_y|·H^{n'}(M_y ∩ B_s(w)) for balls B_s(w) ⊆ B_{ρ_y}(y), and the H^{n'}-density 1 of a C¹ submanifold at each of its points), Θ_{S₀}(w) = |m_y| for every w ∈ M_y ∩ B_{ρ'}(y), so |m_y| = Θ_{S₀}(y) = 1 by (α); S₀ vanishes on the open set B_{ρ'}(y) ∖ M_y, so spt S₀ ∩ B_{ρ'}(y) ⊆ M_y ∩ B_{ρ'}(y), and conversely every point of M_y ∩ B_{ρ'}(y) has density 1 > 0 and lies in spt S₀; hence M ∩ B_{ρ'}(y) = M_y ∩ B_{ρ'}(y) ⊆ A₀ (spt S₀ ⊆ A₀), so M is an embedded C¹ hypersurface of A₀ ∖ {0}; (ii) M is smooth with zero mean curvature (Simon Ch. 5, 7.1, last part, with N = ℝ^P: the varifold of S₀ is stationary in ℝ^P by the sibling minimizing_implies_stationary, integer multiplicity, with density 1 at each y ∈ M, so near each y ∈ M the set M is a C^{q+2,α} graph for every q, and the first variation formula then gives mean curvature 0); (iii) M is a cone; (iv) closure(M) ∖ M = {0}; (v) M is stable in the sense of B.1: M is oriented by the orientation of S₀ (the local orientations m_yξ_{M_y} agree a.e., hence everywhere by continuity); for ζ ∈ C^∞_c(M) let Z be a compactly supported smooth extension of ζν (ν the unit normal of M in A₀) to A₀ ∖ {0}, tangent to A₀, and Φ_t := id + tZ; for small |t|, Φ_{t#}S₀ is an integer multiplicity competitor for S₀ (same boundary, spt(Φ_{t#}S₀ − S₀) ⊆ spt Z compact), so H^{n'}(M ∩ W) ≤ H^{n'}(Φ_t(M ∩ W)) for an open W ⊂⊂ ℝ^P ∖ {0} containing spt Z, and the second variation formula (Simon Ch. 2, 5.12, with H = 0) gives ∫_M(|∇^Mζ|² − |A|²ζ²) dH^{n'} ≥ 0, extended by mollification in charts to compactly supported locally Lipschitz ζ (|A| is continuous on M and supports stay in a fixed compact subset of M), the form used in the printed proof of B.2. (γ) By Simon's Theorem B.2 (Simons [Sim68]) closure(M) is a hyperplane H₀ of A₀. Its printed proof: Simons' identity B.8 and Lemma B.11 (cf. SimonGMT AppendixB/ConeDefect.lean cone_simonsDefect_lower_bound) give, for the minimal cone M, (1/2)Δ_M|A|² + |A|⁴ ≥ 2r^{−2}|A|² + |∇_M|A||²; inserting ζ := |A|ψ into the stability inequality B.1 and integrating by parts yields 2∫_M r^{−2}ψ²|A|² ≤ ∫_M |A|²|∇_Mψ|² for every locally Lipschitz ψ with ∫_M r^{−2}ψ²|A|² < ∞ (first for compactly supported ψ, then by the cut-off functions γ_ε of the printed proof); the choice ψ := r^{1+ε}r₁^{1−n'/2−2ε}, r₁ := max{1, r}, with ε > 0 such that (n'/2 − 2 + ε)² < 2 and (1 + ε)² < 2 (possible exactly because 2 ≤ n' ≤ 6), together with the homogeneity |A(x)|² = r^{−2}|A(x/|x|)|² and the cone formula ∫_M f dH^{n'} = ∫_0^∞ r^{n'−1}∫_{M∩S^{n'}} f(rω) dH^{n'−1}(ω) dr, forces |A| ≡ 0 on M. Then every component of M is an open subset of a hyperplane through 0; since M is relatively closed in A₀ ∖ {0}, embedded, and H ∖ {0} is connected for every hyperplane H of A₀ (n' ≥ 2), M = H₀ ∖ {0} for a single hyperplane H₀.
